sentences.zh: 王重榮

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong

sentences.zh: 王重榮，河中人。

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong was a man of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong was from Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 父縱，鹽州刺史，咸通中有邊功。

translations.literal: His father Zong was military commissioner of Yan Prefecture; in the Xiantong era he had achievements on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Zong had been military commissioner of Yan Prefecture and won distinction on the frontier during the Xiantong reign.

sentences.zh: 重榮以父廕補軍校，與兄重盈俱號驍雄，名璟軍中。

translations.literal: Chongrong entered service as a junior officer by his father's yin privilege; together with his elder brother Chongying they were both called fierce heroes, renowned in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong joined the army as a junior officer through his father's privilege; he and his elder brother Chongying were famed in camp as peerless fighters.

sentences.zh: 廣明初，重榮為河中馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangming, Chongrong was chief adjutant of the Hezhong horse and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangming era he became chief adjutant of Hezhong's combined forces.

sentences.zh: 巢賊據長安，蒲帥李都不能拒，稱臣於賊，賊偽授重榮節度副使。

translations.literal: When Chao's bandits held Chang'an, the Pu commander Li Du could not resist and declared himself a subject of the bandits; the bandits falsely appointed Chongrong deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao held Chang'an, Hezhong's commander Li Du could not hold out and submitted to the rebels, who gave Chongrong a bogus post as deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 河中密邇京師，賊征求無已，軍府疲於供億，賊使百輩，填委傳舍。

translations.literal: Hezhong lay close to the capital; the bandits' exactions were unending; the military government was worn out supplying them; bandit envoys came by the hundred and filled the relay lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong was near the capital, so the rebels never stopped demanding supplies; the command exhausted itself meeting their levies while scores of rebel envoys packed the government inns.

sentences.zh: 重榮謂都曰：「吾以外援未至，詭謀附賊以紓難。

translations.literal: Chongrong said to Du: "Because outside aid had not yet arrived, I used a deceptive plan to attach myself to the bandits in order to ease our distress.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong told Du, "We only pretended to join the rebels because relief had not come yet.

sentences.zh: 今軍府積實，苦被征求，復來收兵，是賊危我也。

translations.literal: Now the military government has accumulated stores, yet we suffer under their exactions; if they come again to take away our troops, the bandits mean to endanger us.
translations.idiomatic: Now the command has stores again, yet they keep squeezing us; if they return to seize our troops, the rebels mean to destroy us.

sentences.zh: 倘不改圖，危亡必矣！

translations.literal: If we do not change our plan, ruin is certain!
translations.idiomatic: Unless we change course, we are finished!

sentences.zh: 請絕橋道，嬰城自固。」

translations.literal: I ask that we cut the bridge routes and hold the city fast behind closed gates."
translations.idiomatic: Let us sever the bridges and defend the walls."

sentences.zh: 都曰：「吾兵微力寡，絕之立見其患。

translations.literal: Du said: "Our troops are few and our strength slight; if we cut them off, disaster will appear at once.
translations.idiomatic: Du replied, "We are too weak; cutting them off would bring disaster immediately.

sentences.zh: 唯公圖之，願以節鉞假公。」

translations.literal: Only you must plan it; I wish to lend you the commissioner's seal and baton.
translations.idiomatic: You must decide. I will lend you my authority as commissioner."

sentences.zh: 翌日，都歸行在，重榮知留後事，乃斬賊使，求援鄰籓。

translations.literal: The next day Du returned to the mobile court; Chongrong took charge of acting commissioner affairs, then beheaded the bandit envoys and sought aid from neighboring circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Du left for the imperial camp and Chongrong took over as acting commissioner; he executed the rebel envoys and appealed to neighboring circuits for help.

sentences.zh: 既而賊將硃溫舟師自同州至，黃鄴之兵自華陰至，數萬攻之。

translations.literal: Before long the bandit general Zhu Wen's river force came from Tong Prefecture and Huang Ye's troops came from Huayin; tens of thousands attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhu Wen brought a fleet from Tong Prefecture and Huang Ye marched from Huayin with tens of thousands to attack.

sentences.zh: 重榮戒勵士眾，大敗之。

translations.literal: Chongrong warned and encouraged the soldiers and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong rallied his men and routed them.

sentences.zh: 獲其兵仗，軍聲益振。

translations.literal: They captured the enemy weapons and the army's renown grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: They seized the enemy arms, and the army's prestige soared.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遂授節鉞，檢校司空。

translations.literal: The court thereupon granted the seal and baton and made him acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The court then invested him as military commissioner and acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時中和元年夏也。

translations.literal: It was summer in the first year of Zhonghe.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the summer of the first year of Zhonghe.

sentences.zh: 俄而忠武監軍楊復光率陳、蔡之師萬人，與重榮合。

translations.literal: Before long the Zhongwu army supervisor Yang Fuguang led ten thousand troops of Chen and Cai and joined with Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yang Fuguang, supervisor of the Zhongwu army, brought ten thousand men from Chen and Cai to join Chongrong.

sentences.zh: 賊將李祥守華州，重榮合勢攻之，擒祥以徇。

translations.literal: The bandit general Li Xiang held Hua Prefecture; Chongrong combined forces to attack him, captured Xiang, and displayed him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Li Xiang held Hua Prefecture; Chongrong attacked in concert, took Xiang prisoner, and paraded him as an example.

sentences.zh: 俄而硃溫以同州降。

translations.literal: Before long Zhu Wen surrendered Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhu Wen surrendered Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賊既失同、華，狂躁益熾。

translations.literal: Once the bandits had lost Tong and Hua, their frenzy grew fiercer still.
translations.idiomatic: After losing Tong and Hua, the rebels grew more desperate and violent.

sentences.zh: 黃巢自率精兵數萬，至梁田坡。

translations.literal: Huang Chao himself led tens of thousands of picked troops to Liangtian Slope.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao personally led tens of thousands of elite troops to Liangtian Slope.

sentences.zh: 時重榮軍華陰南，楊復光在渭北，掎角破賊；

translations.literal: At the time Chongrong's army was south of Huayin and Yang Fuguang was north of the Wei; they took the bandits in pincers and broke them;
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong camped south of Huayin while Fuguang held the north bank of the Wei; attacking in concert they shattered the rebels;

sentences.zh: 出其不意，大敗賊軍，獲其將趙璋。

translations.literal: striking where they did not expect and inflicting a great defeat on the bandit army, capturing their general Zhao Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: caught them by surprise, routed the rebel host, and captured the general Zhao Zhang.

sentences.zh: 巢中流矢而退。

translations.literal: Chao was struck by a stray arrow and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chao took an arrow wound and retreated.

sentences.zh: 而重榮之師，亡耗殆半。

translations.literal: Yet Chongrong's army had lost nearly half its strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chongrong's force had lost nearly half its men.

sentences.zh: 懼賊復來，深憂之。

translations.literal: Fearing the bandits would return, he was deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: He feared the rebels would come again and was deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 謂復光曰：「軍雖小捷，銳旅亡失。

translations.literal: He said to Fuguang: "Though the army had a small victory, our crack troops are lost.
translations.idiomatic: He told Fuguang, "We won a minor victory, but our best troops are gone.

sentences.zh: 萬一賊黨復來，其將何軍以應？

translations.literal: If by chance the bandit host returns, with what army shall we answer them?
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels return, what army will we meet them with?

sentences.zh: 吾之成敗，未可知也。」

translations.literal: Whether we succeed or fail is not yet known."
translations.idiomatic: Our fate is still uncertain."

sentences.zh: 復光曰：「雁門李僕射，與仆家世事舊，其尊人與仆父兄同患難。

translations.literal: Fuguang said: "Vice Minister Li of Yanmen and my family have been old associates for generations; his father and my father and elder brothers shared the same hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang replied, "Li Keyong of Yanmen and my house go back generations; his father and mine faced hardship together.

sentences.zh: 僕射奮不顧身，死義知己。

translations.literal: The Vice Minister throws himself forward without regard for his person and would die for righteousness and for those who know him.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong would risk his life for duty and for a friend.

sentences.zh: 倘得李雁門為援，吾事濟矣。」

translations.literal: If we can obtain Li of Yanmen as aid, our affair will succeed.
translations.idiomatic: If we can win Li Keyong's help, we will prevail."

sentences.zh: 因遣使傳詔征兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent envoys bearing the edict to levy troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent envoys with an imperial summons to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 明年，李克用領兵至，大敗巢賊，收復京城。

translations.literal: The next year Li Keyong led his army thither, inflicted a great defeat on Chao's bandits, and recovered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Li Keyong arrived with his army, crushed Huang Chao's forces, and retook the capital.

sentences.zh: 其倡義啟導之功，實重榮居首。

translations.literal: Of the merit in initiating the righteous cause and opening the way, Chongrong in truth stood first.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who first raised the banner of restoration, Chongrong deserved the foremost credit.

sentences.zh: 京師平，以功檢校太尉、同平章事、瑯邪郡王。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, for his merit he was made acting Grand Marshal, Associate Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Langye commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was secured he was made acting Grand Marshal, chief minister, and Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 光啟元年，僖宗還京。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangqi, Emperor Xizong returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangqi, Emperor Xizong returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 喪亂之後，六軍初復，國藏虛竭。

translations.literal: After the mourning and turmoil, the Six Armies were only beginning to be restored and the national treasury was empty and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After the upheaval the Six Armies were only being rebuilt and the treasury was bare.

sentences.zh: 觀軍容使田令孜奏以安邑、解縣兩池榷課，直屬省司，以充贍給。

translations.literal: Army supervisor Tian Lingzi memorialized that the monopoly levies of the two salt ponds at Anyi and Jie County should pass directly to the provincial offices to supply provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisor Tian Lingzi proposed that salt monopoly revenue from the Anyi and Jie ponds go straight to the central government for supplies.

sentences.zh: 舊事，河中節度兼榷使，每年額輸省課。

translations.literal: By old practice the Hezhong commissioner also held the monopoly commission and each year paid a fixed quota to the provincial levy.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the Hezhong commissioner also controlled the salt monopoly and paid an annual quota to the court.

sentences.zh: 重榮累表論列，既循往例，兼恃大功。

translations.literal: Chongrong repeatedly submitted memorials arguing the case, citing both precedent and his great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong memorialized repeatedly, citing precedent and his outstanding service.

sentences.zh: 令孜不許，奏請移重榮為定州節度。

translations.literal: Lingzi would not agree and memorialized to transfer Chongrong to be commissioner of Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi refused and asked that Chongrong be transferred to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 制下，不奉詔，令孜率禁軍攻之，屯於沙苑，為重榮擊敗之。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued he did not obey; Lingzi led the palace armies to attack him, encamped at Shayuan, and was defeated by Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: When the order came down Chongrong defied it; Lingzi led the palace troops against him at Shayuan and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 十二月，令孜挾天子出幸寶雞，太原聞之，乃與重榮入援京師，遣使迎駕還宮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Lingzi took the Son of Heaven in his grasp and went on progress to Baoji; when Taiyuan heard of it, they joined with Chongrong to enter the capital in aid, sending envoys to welcome the imperial carriage back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Lingzi seized the emperor and fled to Baoji; Li Keyong of Taiyuan joined Chongrong to march on the capital and sent envoys to bring the court home.

sentences.zh: 令孜尤懼，卻劫幸山南。

translations.literal: Lingzi was all the more afraid and turned back to seize the emperor for a progress into Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Lingzi turned back and dragged the emperor south into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 及硃玫立襄王稱制，重榮不受命，會太原之師於河西，以圖興復。

translations.literal: When Zhu Mei set up the Prince of Xiang as regent, Chongrong would not accept the order; he joined the Taiyuan army west of the river to plan restoration.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Mei installed the Prince of Xiang as regent, Chongrong refused to obey; he joined Keyong's forces west of the river to restore the throne.

sentences.zh: 明年，王行瑜殺硃玫，僖宗反正，重榮之忠力居多。

translations.literal: The next year Wang Xingyu killed Zhu Mei; Emperor Xizong was restored to the throne; Chongrong's loyal effort counted for the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Wang Xingyu killed Zhu Mei and Xizong was restored; much of the credit belonged to Chongrong's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 重榮用法稍嚴，季年尤甚。

translations.literal: Chongrong's application of law was somewhat severe, and in his later years it was especially so.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong enforced the law harshly, especially in his last years.

sentences.zh: 部下常行儒者，嘗有所譴罰，深銜之。

translations.literal: His subordinate Chang Xingru had once been punished and bore a deep grudge.
translations.idiomatic: His officer Chang Xingru had once been punished and nursed a deep grievance.

sentences.zh: 光啟三年六月，行儒以兵攻府第，重榮夜出於城外別墅。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Guangqi, Xingru attacked the commissioner's residence with troops; Chongrong fled by night to a villa outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Guangqi year three, Xingru attacked the headquarters; Chongrong slipped out at night to a country villa.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，為行儒所害，行儒乃推重盈為帥。

translations.literal: At dawn he was killed by Xingru; Xingru then pushed Chongying forward as commander.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Xingru killed him and installed Chongying as commander.

sentences.zh: 重盈既立，誅行儒與其黨，安集軍民。

translations.literal: Once Chongying was established, he executed Xingru and his faction and settled the army and the people.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power Chongying executed Xingru and his followers and restored order among troops and civilians.

sentences.zh: 乾寧初，重盈卒，軍府推行軍司馬王珂為留後。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianning, Chongying died; the military government pushed the acting army marshal Wang Ke as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianning, Chongying died; the command installed army marshal Wang Ke as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 重盈子珙，時為陜帥，瑤為絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Chongying's son Gong was at the time commander of Shan, and Yao was prefect of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chongying's son Gong was military commissioner of Shan, and Yao was prefect of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 珂即重榮兄重簡子，出繼重榮。

translations.literal: Ke was the son of Chongrong's elder brother Chongjian and had been given in adoption to Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was the son of Chongrong's brother Chongjian and had been adopted by Chongrong.

sentences.zh: 由是爭為蒲帥。

translations.literal: Thereupon they contended for the post of Pu commander.
translations.idiomatic: A struggle ensued over who would command Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 瑤、珙上章論列，又與硃溫書云：「珂非吾兄弟，家之蒼頭也。

translations.literal: Yao and Gong submitted memorials arguing the case, and also wrote to Zhu Wen saying: "Ke is not our brother but a household slave.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Gong memorialized the court and wrote Zhu Wen: "Ke is no brother of ours but a household slave.

sentences.zh: 小字蟲兒，安得繼嗣？」

translations.literal: His childhood name was 'Little Worm'—how can he inherit?"
translations.idiomatic: His pet name was 'Little Worm'—how can he inherit the command?"

sentences.zh: 珂上章云：「亡父有興復之功。」

translations.literal: Ke submitted a memorial saying: "My late father had merit in restoring the dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: Ke replied in a memorial: "My late father restored the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 遣使求援於太原，太原保薦於朝。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to seek aid from Taiyuan; Taiyuan recommended him at court.
translations.idiomatic: He sent to Taiyuan for support, and Keyong recommended him at court.

sentences.zh: 珙厚結王行瑜、李茂貞、韓建為援，三鎮互相表薦。

translations.literal: Gong bound himself closely to Wang Xingyu, Li Maozhen, and Han Jian as allies; the three circuits mutually recommended one another in memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Gong cultivated Wang Xingyu, Li Maozhen, and Han Jian as allies; the three circuits backed one another in memorials.

sentences.zh: 昭宗詔諭之曰：「吾以太原與重榮有再造之功，已俞其奏矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong issued an edict instructing them: "Because Taiyuan and Chongrong had the merit of recreating the dynasty, I have already approved their memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong told them: "Taiyuan and Chongrong remade the dynasty; I have already approved Keyong's request."

sentences.zh: 故明年五月，茂貞等三人率兵入覲，賊害時政，請以河中授珙。

translations.literal: Therefore in the fifth month of the following year Maozhen and the other three led troops to audience at court, harmed the politics of the time, and asked that Hezhong be given to Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The next fifth month Maozhen and the others marched on the capital, bullied the court, and demanded Hezhong for Gong.

sentences.zh: 珙、瑤連兵攻河中。

translations.literal: Gong and Yao joined forces to attack Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Gong and Yao attacked Hezhong together.

sentences.zh: 李克用怒，出師討三鎮。

translations.literal: Li Keyong was enraged and marched out to punish the three circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong marched out in anger to punish the three circuits.

sentences.zh: 瑤、珙兵退，克用拔絳州，斬瑤，乃師於渭北。

translations.literal: Yao and Gong's troops withdrew; Keyong took Jiang Prefecture and beheaded Yao, then led his army north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Gong retreated; Keyong seized Jiang Prefecture, executed Yao, and camped north of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 天子以珂為河中節度，授以旄鉞，仍充供軍糧料使。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven made Ke military commissioner of Hezhong, granted him the banner and axe, and also appointed him provisioner for army grain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor confirmed Ke as Hezhong commissioner, invested him with full authority, and made him army provisioner.

sentences.zh: 既誅王行瑜，克用以女妻之。

translations.literal: After Wang Xingyu was executed, Keyong gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingyu was killed, Keyong gave Ke his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 珂親至太原、太原令李嗣昭將兵助珂攻珙，珙每戰頻敗。

translations.literal: Ke went in person to Taiyuan; Taiyuan ordered Li Sizhao to lead troops to help Ke attack Gong; Gong was defeated in battle after battle.
translations.idiomatic: Ke went to Taiyuan in person; Keyong sent Li Sizhao to help him attack Gong, who lost battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 珙性慘刻，人有逾犯，必斬首置於座前，言笑自若，部下鹹苦之。

translations.literal: Gong's nature was cruel and harsh; if anyone overstepped, he would certainly behead him and set the head before his seat, then speak and laugh as if at ease; the subordinates all suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was brutal: any offender was beheaded and the head set before him while he chatted on; his men suffered terribly.

sentences.zh: 因其削弱，皆懷離叛。

translations.literal: Because he was weakened, all harbored thoughts of desertion.
translations.idiomatic: As his power waned, his followers turned against him.

sentences.zh: 光化二年六月，部將李璠殺珙，自稱留後。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Guanghua, the subordinate officer Li Fan killed Gong and declared himself acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Guanghua year two, Li Fan killed Gong and proclaimed himself acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 光化末，朱溫初伏鎮、定，將圖關輔，屬劉季述廢立之際，京師俶擾。

translations.literal: At the end of Guanghua, Zhu Wen had just subdued Zhen and Ding and was about to scheme for the Guanfu region; it fell at the time of Liu Jishu's deposition and enthronement, and the capital was in sudden turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Guanghua, Zhu Wen had just taken Zhen and Ding and aimed at the capital region; during Liu Jishu's coup the court was thrown into chaos.

sentences.zh: 崔胤潛乞師於汴，以圖反正。

translations.literal: Cui Yin secretly begged troops from Bian to plan restoration of the proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin secretly asked Bian for troops to restore the throne.

sentences.zh: 溫謂其將張存敬、侯言曰：「王珂恃太原之勢，侮慢籓鄰，骨肉相殘，自大其事，爾為我持一繩以縛之。」

translations.literal: Wen said to his generals Zhang Cunjing and Hou Yan: "Wang Ke relies on Taiyuan's power, insults and looks down on neighboring circuits, lets kin slaughter kin, and magnifies his own affair—take a rope for me and bind him."
translations.idiomatic: Wen told Zhang Cunjing and Hou Yan, "Wang Ke leans on Taiyuan, insults his neighbors, lets kin kill kin, and swells with pride—go take a rope and bind him for me."

sentences.zh: 存敬等率兵數萬渡河，由含山出其不意，天復元年正月，兵攻晉、絳。

translations.literal: Cunjing and the others led tens of thousands of troops across the river, came out by Hanshan to take them unawares; in the first month of the first year of Tianfu they attacked Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Cunjing crossed the river with tens of thousands, struck from Hanshan by surprise, and in the first month of Tianfu year one attacked Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 珂將絳州刺史陶建釗、晉州刺史張漢瑜既無備，即開門降。

translations.literal: Ke's generals Tao Jianzhao, prefect of Jiang, and Zhang Hanyu, prefect of Jin, were unprepared and at once opened the gates and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Ke's prefects Tao Jianzhao of Jiang and Zhang Hanyu of Jin were caught unprepared and surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 溫令別將何絪守晉州，扼其援路。

translations.literal: Wen ordered the separate commander He Yin to hold Jin Prefecture and choke off their route of relief.
translations.idiomatic: Wen left He Yin to hold Jin Prefecture and block relief from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 二月，存敬大軍逼河中，珂遣告急於太原。

translations.literal: In the second month Cunjing's great army pressed Hezhong; Ke sent urgent word to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Cunjing's main force closed on Hezhong; Ke sent desperate appeals to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 晉、絳既當兵沖，援師不能進。

translations.literal: Jin and Jiang now lay in the path of the armies, and relief troops could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: With Jin and Jiang in enemy hands, relief could not get through.

sentences.zh: 珂妻書告太原曰：「賊勢攻逼，朝夕為俘囚，乞食大梁，大人安忍不救？」

translations.literal: Ke's wife wrote to Taiyuan: "The bandit host presses the attack; any day we may be captives, begging food in Great Liang—how can you, sir, bear not to save us?"
translations.idiomatic: Ke's wife wrote Keyong: "The enemy is closing in; we will be prisoners any day, begging bread in Liang—how can you refuse to save us?"

sentences.zh: 克用曰：「賊阻前途，眾寡不敵，救則與爾兩亡。

translations.literal: Keyong said: "The bandits block the road ahead; our numbers cannot match theirs; if I rescue you, we perish together.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong replied, "The enemy blocks the road; we are too few; if I march to save you, we both die.

sentences.zh: 可與王郎歸朝廷。」

translations.literal: You may go with Lord Wang back to the court."
translations.idiomatic: Take your husband and submit to the court."

sentences.zh: 珂計無從出，即謀歸京師。

translations.literal: Ke had no plan left and thereupon plotted to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: With no other option, Ke planned to flee to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又使人告李茂貞曰：「聖上初返正，詔籓鎮無相侵伐，同匡王室。

translations.literal: He also sent someone to tell Li Maozhen: "When the Sage Lord had just been restored to the throne, he decreed that the circuits should not invade one another but together support the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Li Maozhen: "When the emperor was restored, he ordered the circuits not to attack one another but to uphold the throne together.

sentences.zh: 硃公不顧國家約束，卒遣賊臣，急攻敝邑，則硃公之心可見矣！

translations.literal: Lord Zhu paid no heed to the state's restraints and finally sent a treacherous minister to press the attack on our poor city—then Lord Zhu's heart can be seen!
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen ignored the court's order and sent his generals to crush us—his ambition is plain!

sentences.zh: 敝邑若亡，則同、華、邠、岐非諸君所能保也。

translations.literal: If our poor city perishes, then Tong, Hua, Bin, and Qi are not what you gentlemen can preserve.
translations.idiomatic: If we fall, you cannot hold Tong, Hua, Bin, and Qi either.

sentences.zh: 天子神器，拱手而授人矣！

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's sacred regalia will be handed over with folded arms to another!
translations.idiomatic: The throne itself will be surrendered without a fight!

sentences.zh: 此自然之勢也。

translations.literal: This is the natural course of events.
translations.idiomatic: That is how matters must unfold.

sentences.zh: 公可與華州令公早出精銳固潼關，以應敝邑。

translations.literal: You, sir, may join the Lord of Hua Prefecture in early dispatch of picked troops to hold Tong Pass firm and respond to our poor city.
translations.idiomatic: March with the commander of Hua and seize Tong Pass with elite troops to relieve us.

sentences.zh: 仆自量不武，請於公之西偏求為鎮守，此地請公有之。

translations.literal: I measure myself as not martial enough and ask to be stationed on your western flank; as for this place, I ask that you, sir, take it.
translations.idiomatic: I am no fighter; let me hold a post on your western flank while you take Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 關西安危，國祚延促，系公此舉也。」

translations.literal: The security of Guanxi and the prolongation of the dynastic fortune depend on this move of yours."
translations.idiomatic: The fate of the northwest and the dynasty rests on what you do now."

sentences.zh: 茂貞不答。

translations.literal: Maozhen did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen did not answer.

sentences.zh: 珂勢蹙，將渡河歸京師，人情離合。

translations.literal: Ke's situation was pressed tight; he was about to cross the river and return to the capital, and men's hearts were divided between staying and leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was cornered and prepared to cross the river to the capital; morale wavered between loyalty and desertion.

sentences.zh: 時河橋毀圮，淩澌鯁塞，舟楫難濟。

translations.literal: At the time the river bridge was ruined and broken ice choked the current; boats and oars could hardly cross.
translations.idiomatic: The river bridge was wrecked and floes blocked the crossing; boats could hardly get through.

sentences.zh: 珂族艤舟有日。

translations.literal: Ke's clan had moored boats for days.
translations.idiomatic: Ke's family had waited days with boats ready.

sentences.zh: 珂夜自慰諭守陴者，默然無應。

translations.literal: Ke by night consoled and instructed the wall defenders himself; they were silent and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Ke went among the wall guards at night to rally them; they answered only with silence.

sentences.zh: 牙將劉訓夜半至珂寢門，珂叱之曰：「兵欲反耶？」

translations.literal: Army officer Liu Xun came at midnight to Ke's sleeping-chamber door; Ke rebuked him, saying, "Are the troops about to rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: At midnight adjutant Liu Xun appeared at Ke's chamber door; Ke snapped, "Are the men mutinying?"

sentences.zh: 訓解衣袒臂曰：「公茍懷疑，訓請斷臂。」

translations.literal: Xun stripped his upper garment and bared his arms, saying, "If Your Lordship still doubts me, Xun asks to sever his arm."
translations.idiomatic: Xun bared his arms and said, "If you still doubt me, cut off my arm."

sentences.zh: 珂曰：「事勢如何，計將安出？」

translations.literal: Ke said, "How stands the situation—what plan do you propose?"
translations.idiomatic: Ke asked, "What's our position, and what do you advise?"

sentences.zh: 訓曰：「若夜出整棹待濟，人必爭舟。

translations.literal: Xun said, "If we sort the boats at night and wait to cross, men will surely fight over the craft.
translations.idiomatic: Xun said, "If we ready the boats tonight and wait to embark, the men will fight for seats.

sentences.zh: 茍一夫鴟張，其禍莫測。

translations.literal: Should one man swagger and seize control, the calamity cannot be foretold.
translations.idiomatic: Let one hothead take charge and no one can say what disaster follows.

sentences.zh: 不如俟明旦，以情諭三軍，願從者必半，然後登舟赴闕，可以前濟。

translations.literal: Better wait until dawn, speak plainly to the three armies, those willing to follow will surely be half, then board boats and go to the court—it can be done in good order.
translations.idiomatic: Better wait until morning, explain ourselves to the whole army—half will surely come with us—then board for the capital and cross in an orderly way.

sentences.zh: 不然，則召諸將校，且為款狀，以緩賊軍，徐圖向背，策之上也。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, summon the officers, for the moment make a show of submission to slow the bandit army, and gradually work out where loyalties lie—that would be the best stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Or call the officers, feign submission to stall the enemy, and slowly sound out who stands where—that's the soundest course."

sentences.zh: 珂然之，即登城謂存敬曰：「吾於汴王有家世事分，公宜退舍。

translations.literal: Ke approved; he at once mounted the wall and said to Cunjing, "I and the Prince of Bian have a family bond of generations; you should withdraw camp.
translations.idiomatic: Ke agreed, climbed the wall, and told Cunjing, "The Prince of Bian and I are old family allies—you should pull back.

sentences.zh: 俟汴王至，吾自聽命。」

translations.literal: When the Prince of Bian arrives, I myself will await his orders."
translations.idiomatic: When the prince comes, I will obey whatever he commands."

sentences.zh: 存敬即日退舍。

translations.literal: Cunjing that same day withdrew camp.
translations.idiomatic: Cunjing withdrew the same day.

sentences.zh: 三月，朱溫自洛陽至，先哭於重榮之墓，悲不自勝，陳辭致祭，蒲人聞之感悅。

translations.literal: In the third month Zhu Wen came from Luoyang; first he wept at Chongrong's tomb, grief beyond self-control, set forth words and made offerings; the people of Pu heard it and were moved with pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Zhu Wen arrived from Luoyang, wept first at Chongrong's grave until he could scarcely stand, and offered a full funeral address; the people of Hezhong were deeply touched.

sentences.zh: 珂欲面縛牽羊以見。

translations.literal: Ke wished to go out with bound hands leading a sheep to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Ke meant to submit with the ritual of bound hands and a leading sheep.

sentences.zh: 溫報曰：「太師阿舅之恩，何時可忘耶？

translations.literal: Wen replied, "The kindness of the Grand Preceptor, my uncle by marriage—when could it be forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: Wen answered, "How could I ever forget my father-in-law the Grand Preceptor's kindness?

sentences.zh: 郎君若以亡國之禮相見，黃泉其謂我何？」

translations.literal: If you, young lord, meet me with the rites of a fallen state, what will the Yellow Springs say of me?"
translations.idiomatic: If you greet me as though you were a conquered prince, what will my dead kin think of me?"

sentences.zh: 及珂出，迎之於路，握手歔欷，聯轡而入。

translations.literal: When Ke came out, Wen met him on the road; they clasped hands and sobbed, rein to rein they entered together.
translations.idiomatic: When Ke emerged, Wen met him on the road; they clasped hands weeping and rode in side by side.

sentences.zh: 居半月，以存敬守河中，珂舉家徙於汴。

translations.literal: After half a month, Cunjing was left to garrison Hezhong; Ke moved his whole household to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: After a fortnight Wen left Cunjing in charge of Hezhong and relocated Ke's entire family to Bian.

sentences.zh: 後溫令珂入覲，遣人殺之於華州傳舍。

translations.literal: Later Wen ordered Ke to come to audience; he sent men to kill him at a relay lodge in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wen summoned Ke to court and had him killed at a relay inn in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 自重榮初帥河中，傳至珂二十年。

translations.literal: From when Chongrong first commanded Hezhong, the line passed to Ke—twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: From Chongrong's first command of Hezhong to Ke's end was twenty years.

sentences.zh: 王處存

translations.literal: =Wang Chucun=
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun

sentences.zh: 王處存，京兆萬年縣勝業裏人。

translations.literal: Wang Chucun was a man of Shengye Lane, Wannian County, Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun was from Shengye Lane in Wannian, capital district of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 世隸神策軍，為京師富族，財產數百萬。

translations.literal: For generations his family served the Shence Army; they were a wealthy clan of the capital, with property worth millions.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had long served in the Shence Army and ranked among the capital's richest houses, with wealth in the millions.

sentences.zh: 父宗，自軍校累至檢校司空、金吾大將軍、左街使，遙領興元節度。

translations.literal: His father Zong rose from army school officer through cumulative posts to acting minister of justice, grand general of the Golden Crow Guards, and Left Street commissioner, with titular command of the Xingyuan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Zong had risen from a junior officer to acting minister of justice, commander of the Golden Crow Guards, commissioner of the Left Street, and nominal military governor of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 宗善興利，乘時貿易，由是富擬王者，仕宦因貲而貴，侯服玉食，僮奴萬指。

translations.literal: Zong was skilled at gaining profit and traded on opportune moments; thereby his wealth rivaled kings, officeholders grew noble through wealth, he wore noble robes and jade fare, his servants and bondsmen numbered in the ten thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zong knew how to turn a profit and traded on every opening until his riches rivaled a king's; offices bought prestige, and he lived like royalty with tens of thousands of servants at his beck.

sentences.zh: 處存起家右軍鎮使，累至驍衛將軍、左軍巡使。

translations.literal: Chucun began his career as deputy commander of the Right Army, and rose through the ranks to general of the Martial Guards and patrol commissioner of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: Chucun began in the Right Army, rose to general of the Martial Guards, and became patrol commissioner of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 乾符六年十月，檢校刑部尚書、義武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year of Qianfu he was acting minister of justice and military commissioner of the Yiwu army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Qianfu year six he received acting rank as minister of justice and command of the Yiwu army.

sentences.zh: 明年，黃巢犯闕，僖宗出幸。

translations.literal: The next year Huang Chao assaulted the palace precincts and Emperor Xizong went on tour.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Huang Chao stormed the capital and Emperor Xizong fled.

sentences.zh: 處存號哭累日，不俟詔命，即率本軍入援。

translations.literal: Chucun wailed for many days; without awaiting imperial order he at once led his own army to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Chucun mourned aloud for days and, without waiting for orders, marched his army to the emperor's aid.

sentences.zh: 遣二千人間道往山南，衛從車駕。

translations.literal: He sent two thousand men by a hidden route toward Shannan to guard and follow the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He sent two thousand men by back roads into Shannan to escort the imperial train.

sentences.zh: 時李都守河中降賊，會王重榮斬偽使，通使於處存，乃同盟誓師，營於渭北。

translations.literal: At that time Li Du held Hezhong and submitted to the bandits; then Wang Chongrong beheaded a false envoy, opened communication with Chucun, and they swore alliance and mustered troops, encamping north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Du still held Hezhong for the rebels until Chongrong killed a rebel envoy and opened talks with Chucun; the two allied, took their oaths, and camped north of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 時巢賊僭號，天下籓鎮，多受其偽命，唯鄭畋守鳳翔，鄭從讜守太原。

translations.literal: At that time Chao's bandits usurped titles; circuit commands across the realm mostly accepted their false commissions—only Zheng Tian held Fengxiang and Zheng Congdang held Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao had proclaimed himself emperor and most governors accepted his commissions; only Zheng Tian at Fengxiang and Zheng Congdang at Taiyuan stood firm.

sentences.zh: 處存、王重榮首倡義舉，以招太原。

translations.literal: Chucun and Wang Chongrong first raised the righteous banner to draw in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chucun and Chongrong were first to raise the loyal standard and win Taiyuan over.

sentences.zh: 俄而鄭畋破賊前鋒，王鐸自行在至，故諸鎮翻然改圖，以出勤王之師。

translations.literal: Before long Zheng Tian defeated the bandits' vanguard, Wang Duo came from the imperial entourage, and so the various commands suddenly changed their plans and sent out troops to relieve the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zheng Tian broke the rebel van, Wang Duo arrived from the imperial camp, and commands across the land turned at once to march armies for the throne.

sentences.zh: 中和元年四月，涇原行軍唐弘夫敗賊將林言、尚讓軍，乘勝進逼京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Zhonghe, Tang Hongfu of the Jingyuan field army defeated the armies of the bandit generals Lin Yan and Shang Rang and pressed the advantage toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Zhonghe year one, Tang Hongfu of Jingyuan routed Lin Yan and Shang Rang and drove toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 處存自渭北親選驍卒五千，皆以白繻為號，夜入京城。

translations.literal: Chucun from north of the Wei personally chose five thousand elite troops, all using white silk as their mark, and entered the capital by night.
translations.idiomatic: Chucun picked five thousand picked men north of the Wei, all wearing white badges, and entered the city at night.

sentences.zh: 賊已遁去。

translations.literal: The bandits had already fled away.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were already gone.

sentences.zh: 京師故人見處存，遮道慟哭，歡呼塞路。

translations.literal: Old acquaintances in the capital saw Chucun, blocked the road weeping, and cheers filled the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Old friends in the capital barred his path in tears while cheers choked every street.

sentences.zh: 軍人皆釋兵，爭據第宅，坊市少年多帶白號雜軍。

translations.literal: The soldiers all laid down weapons and scrambled to seize mansions; young men of the wards mostly wore white marks and mingled with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers threw down their arms to seize great houses, and ward youths in white badges mixed freely among the troops.

sentences.zh: 翌日，賊偵知，自灞上復襲京師，市人以為王師，歡呼迎之。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits' scouts learned of it; from Bashang they again struck the capital; townspeople thought it was the royal army and cheered to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Next day rebel scouts found out; rebels swept down from Bashang again, and townsfolk mistook them for imperial troops and cheered them in.

sentences.zh: 處存為賊所迫，收軍還營。

translations.literal: Chucun was pressed by the bandits and drew his army back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by the rebels, Chucun pulled his men back to camp.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，召集兩市丁壯七八萬，並殺之，血流成渠。

translations.literal: The bandits were enraged; they gathered seven or eighty thousand able-bodied men of the two markets and killed them all; blood formed channels.
translations.idiomatic: In fury they rounded up seventy or eighty thousand market laborers and slaughtered them until blood ran in ditches.

sentences.zh: 處存家在京師，世受國恩，以賊寇未平，鑾輿出狩，每言及時事，未嘗不喑嗚流涕，諸軍義之。

translations.literal: Chucun's family was in the capital and for generations had received the state's grace; because the bandits were not yet pacified and the imperial carriage was on tour, whenever he spoke of current affairs he never failed to choke and weep; the armies honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Chucun's family lived in the capital on generations of imperial favor; with rebels still abroad and the emperor in exile, he wept whenever affairs of state were mentioned, and the troops revered him for it.

sentences.zh: 前後遣使十輩迎李克用，既奕世姻好，特相款昵。

translations.literal: Before and after he sent ten missions of envoys to welcome Li Keyong; they were marriage kin for generations and treated each other with especial warmth.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys again and again—ten missions in all—to bring Li Keyong south; bound by generations of marriage ties, the two treated each other with deep affection.

sentences.zh: 洎收京師，王鐸第其功；

translations.literal: When the capital was recovered, Wang Duo ranked their merits;
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was retaken, Wang Duo graded their achievements:

sentences.zh: 勤王舉義，處存為之最；

translations.literal: in raising troops to relieve the throne, Chucun stood first;
translations.idiomatic: for rallying loyal armies, Chucun ranked first;

sentences.zh: 收城破賊，克用為之最。

translations.literal: in recovering the city and breaking the bandits, Keyong stood first.
translations.idiomatic: for retaking the city and crushing the rebels, Keyong ranked first.

sentences.zh: 以功檢校司空。

translations.literal: For merit he was made acting grand guardian.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made acting grand guardian of state.

sentences.zh: 後又遣大將張公慶率勁兵三千，合諸軍滅賊巢於泰山，以功檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Later he again sent his great general Zhang Gongqing leading three thousand crack troops; together with other armies they destroyed Chao's nest on Mount Tai; for merit he was made acting minister mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He later sent Zhang Gongqing with three thousand elite troops to join other forces and wipe out Chao's remnant on Mount Tai, earning promotion to acting minister mentor.

sentences.zh: 田令孜討王重榮，詔處存為河中節度。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi campaigned against Wang Chongrong and ordered Chucun as military commissioner of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Lingzi moved against Chongrong, the court named Chucun military governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 處存上章申理，言：「重榮無罪，有大功於國，不宜輕有除改，以搖籓鎮之心。」

translations.literal: Chucun submitted a memorial pleading the case, saying, "Chongrong is without guilt and has great merit to the state; he should not lightly be removed and replaced, lest the hearts of the circuit commands be shaken."
translations.idiomatic: Chucun memorialized in Chongrong's defense: "He is innocent and has rendered great service; to replace him lightly would unsettle every frontier command."

sentences.zh: 初，幽、鎮兩籓，兵甲強盛，易定於其間，疲於侵寇。

translations.literal: In the beginning the two circuits of You and Zhen had strong armor and weapons; Yiding lay between them and was worn down by invasion and raids.
translations.idiomatic: Yiding lay squeezed between mighty Youzhou and Zhenzhou and had long suffered their raids.

sentences.zh: 及匡威得誌驕盈，恆欲兼並之。

translations.literal: When Kuangwei got his wish he grew arrogant and overbearing, constantly wishing to annex it.
translations.idiomatic: Once Kuangwei got his way he grew arrogant and constantly sought to swallow the territory.

sentences.zh: 賴與太原姻好，每為之援。

translations.literal: They relied on marriage ties with Taiyuan and each time received support from there.
translations.idiomatic: They relied on marriage ties with Taiyuan, which backed them each time.

sentences.zh: 處存亦睦鄰以禮，優撫軍民，折節下士，人多歸之，以至抗衡列鎮。

translations.literal: Chucun also treated neighboring states with courtesy, favored and comforted troops and people, lowered himself to honor scholar-officers—many came to him, so that he could balance the ranks of the commands.
translations.idiomatic: Chucun courted his neighbors politely, cared for soldiers and civilians alike, and humbled himself before men of talent until people flocked to him and his command could stand equal to the great circuits.

sentences.zh: 累加侍中、檢校太尉。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to palace attendant and acting grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant and then acting grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年九月卒，年六十五，贈太子太師，謚曰忠肅。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Qianning he died at age sixty-five; he was posthumously made heir-apparent grand preceptor with the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of Qianning year two, aged sixty-five, and was posthumously honored as heir-apparent grand preceptor with the temple name Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 三軍以河朔舊事，推其子副大使郜為留後。

translations.literal: The three armies by the old Hebei custom installed his son, vice commissioner Gao, as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Following Hebei custom, the army installed his son Gao, the vice commissioner, as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 朝廷從而命之。

translations.literal: The court followed with the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The court confirmed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 授以旄鉞，尋加檢校司空、同平章事，累至太保。

translations.literal: He was granted the battle-axe and pennant; soon after acting grand guardian and fellow of the Secretariat; he rose step by step to grand guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Gao received the commissioner insignia, soon became acting grand guardian and chancellor, and rose to grand guardian of state.

sentences.zh: 光化三年七月，汴將張存敬進寇幽州，旋入祁溝。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Guanghua, the Bian general Zhang Cunjing advanced to raid You Prefecture and soon entered Qigou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Guanghua year three, Zhang Cunjing of Bian marched on Youzhou and soon pushed into Qigou.

sentences.zh: 郜遣馬步都將王處直將兵拒之，為存敬所敗，退營沙河。

translations.literal: Gao sent his horse-and-foot commander Wang Chuzhi to lead troops to resist; he was defeated by Cunjing and withdrew camp to Shahe.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent Wang Chuzhi with the combined forces to resist; Cunjing defeated him and drove him back to camp at Shahe.

sentences.zh: 汴人進擊，營於懷德驛。

translations.literal: The Bian men pressed the attack and encamped at Huaide post station.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian army pressed on and pitched camp at Huaide Station.

sentences.zh: 處直之眾奔撓，城中大恐。

translations.literal: Chuzhi's troops broke and scattered in flight; inside the city there was great terror.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi's men broke and fled; panic gripped the city.

sentences.zh: 十月，郜委城攜族奔於太原，太原累表授檢校太尉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Gao abandoned the city, took his clan, and fled to Taiyuan; Taiyuan repeatedly memorialized to appoint him acting grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Gao abandoned the city and fled with his clan to Taiyuan, which memorialized repeatedly to make him acting grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 天復初，卒於晉陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu he died at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianfu era he died at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 郜弟 鄴其弟鄴，克用以女妻之，歷嵐、石、沔三州刺史、大同軍防禦使。

translations.literal: Gao's younger brother Ye—Keyong gave him a daughter in marriage; he served successively as prefect of Lan, Shi, and Mian and as defensive commissioner of the Datong army.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's younger brother Ye married a daughter of Keyong and served in turn as prefect of Lan, Shi, and Mian and as defensive commissioner of Datong.

sentences.zh: 天祐中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Tianyou era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Tianyou period.

sentences.zh: 處存母弟 處直處直，字允明，處存母弟也。

translations.literal: Chucun's younger brother by the same mother—Chuzhi, courtesy name Yunming, was Chucun's younger brother by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Chucun's uterine brother Wang Chuzhi, styled Yunming, was born of the same mother.

sentences.zh: 初為定州後院軍都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: He first served as commander knowing horses and troops of the Dingzhou rear-garrison army.
translations.idiomatic: He began as commander of the Dingzhou rear-garrison forces.

sentences.zh: 汴人入寇，處直拒戰不利而退；

translations.literal: When Bian men entered to raid, Chuzhi resisted but the battle went badly and he withdrew;
translations.idiomatic: When Bian troops invaded, Chuzhi fought and withdrew after a defeat;

sentences.zh: 三軍大噪，推處直為帥。

translations.literal: the three armies raised a great clamor and installed Chuzhi as commander.
translations.idiomatic: the army clamored and made Chuzhi their leader.

sentences.zh: 及郜出奔，乃權留後事。

translations.literal: When Gao fled out, he then held acting charge of the commissioner's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao fled, he took acting command of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 汴將張存敬攻城，梯沖雲合，處直登城呼曰：「敝邑於朝廷未嘗不忠，於籓鄰未嘗失禮，不虞君之涉吾地，何也？」

translations.literal: The Bian general Zhang Cunjing besieged the city; scaling ladders and battering rams clouded together; Chuzhi mounted the wall and called out, "Our humble district has never been disloyal to the court, never failed in courtesy toward neighboring circuits—we did not expect you, lord, to tread our land; why?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cunjing besieged the city with ladders and rams massed thick; Chuzhi mounted the wall and shouted, "We have never wronged the court or our neighbors—why have you entered our land uninvited?"

sentences.zh: 朱溫遣人報之曰：「何以附太原而弱鄰道？」

translations.literal: Zhu Wen sent a man to reply, "Why lean on Taiyuan and weaken a neighboring circuit?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen sent word: "Why do you cling to Taiyuan and undermine your neighbors?"

sentences.zh: 處直報曰：「吾兄與太原同時立勛王室，地又親鄰，修好往來，常道也。

translations.literal: Chuzhi replied, "My elder brother and Taiyuan at the same time established merit for the royal house; our lands are moreover kin-neighbors; maintaining friendly contact is the constant way.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi answered, "My brother and Taiyuan earned their honors together for the throne; our regions are close kin and allies—friendly ties are only proper.

sentences.zh: 請從此改圖。」

translations.literal: I ask from here to change course."
translations.idiomatic: From now on we will change course."

sentences.zh: 溫許之。

translations.literal: Wen assented.
translations.idiomatic: Wen agreed.

sentences.zh: 仍歸罪於孔目吏梁問，出絹十萬匹，牛酒以犒汴軍。

translations.literal: He also shifted blame onto the clerical officer Liang Wen, sent out one hundred thousand bolts of silk, and oxen and wine to reward the Bian army.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed his clerk Liang Wen, sent a hundred thousand bolts of silk, and furnished oxen and wine to feast the Bian troops.

sentences.zh: 存敬修盟而退。

translations.literal: Cunjing renewed the alliance and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Cunjing sealed a new pact and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 溫因表授旄鉞，檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: Wen thereupon memorialized to grant the battle-axe and pennant and acting left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Wen memorialized to invest him with commissioner rank and acting left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 天祐元年，加太保，封太原王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianyou he was advanced to grand guardian and enfeoffed as King of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou year one he was made grand guardian and enfeoffed as King of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 後仕偽梁，授北平王，檢校太尉。

translations.literal: Later he served the bogus Liang, was made Prince of Northern Ping and acting grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted to Zhu Wen's Liang and received the title Prince of Northern Ping with acting grand commandant rank.

sentences.zh: 不數歲，復於莊宗。

translations.literal: Within a few years he returned allegiance to Zhuangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he returned to Li Cunxu's cause.

sentences.zh: 後十餘年，為其子都廢歸私第，尋卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: More than ten years later his son Du deposed him and sent him back to a private residence; soon he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: A decade later his son Du removed him to private quarters; he died soon after, aged sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 諸葛爽

translations.literal: =Zhuge Shuang=
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Shuang

sentences.zh: 諸葛爽，青州博昌人。

translations.literal: Zhuge Shuang was a man of Bochang, Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Shuang was from Bochang in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 役屬縣為伍伯，為令所笞，乃棄役，以裏謳自給。

translations.literal: He served the subprefecture as a ward headman and was flogged by the magistrate; he then abandoned his service and supported himself by village songs.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a local ward officer until the magistrate had him beaten; he quit the post and lived on folk songs in the lanes.

sentences.zh: 會龐勛之亂，乃委身為徐卒，累軍功至小校。

translations.literal: When Pang Xun's rebellion arose, he threw in his lot as a Xuzhou soldier and through cumulative military merit rose to junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: During Pang Xun's revolt he enlisted as a soldier in Xuzhou and rose by merit to junior officer.

sentences.zh: 官軍討徐，龐勛勢蹙，率百余人與泗州守將陽群歸國。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Xuzhou, Pang Xun's power was cramped; he led more than a hundred men with Sizhou garrison commander Yang Qun to return to the state.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial forces closed on Xuzhou and Pang Xun's cause collapsed, he led a hundred men with Sizhou's Yang Qun back to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 累授汝州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed defensive commissioner of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to defensive commissioner of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李琢為招討使，討沙阤於雲州，表爽為副。

translations.literal: Li Zhuo was expedition commissioner campaigning against the Shatuo at Yun Prefecture; he memorialized Shuang as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhuo was expedition commissioner against the Shatuo in Yunzhou, he named Shuang his deputy.

sentences.zh: 廣明元年，賊陷京師，詔爽率代北行營兵馬，赴難關中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangming the bandits took the capital; an edict ordered Shuang to lead the northern frontier mobile army to rush relief to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangming year one, after rebels took Chang'an, Shuang was ordered to lead northern frontier troops to rescue the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 爽軍屯櫟陽。

translations.literal: Shuang's army encamped at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang's army camped at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 潼關不守，車駕出幸，爽乃降賊。

translations.literal: Tong Pass could not be held; the imperial carriage went on tour; Shuang then submitted to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Pass fell and the emperor fled, Shuang surrendered to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 巢以爽為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: Chao made Shuang military commissioner of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao made him military governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 巢賊敗，復表歸國，進位檢校司徒。

translations.literal: When Chao's bandits were defeated, he again memorialized to return to the state and was advanced to acting minister mentor.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels fell, he petitioned to rejoin the Tang and was promoted to acting minister mentor.

sentences.zh: 時魏博韓簡軍勢方盛。

translations.literal: At that time Han Jian of Weibo's military power was just flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian of Weibo then commanded a powerful army.

sentences.zh: 中和元年四月，魏人攻河陽，大敗爽軍於修武，爽棄城遁走。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Zhonghe the Weibo men attacked Heyang, greatly defeated Shuang's army at Xiuwu, and Shuang abandoned the city and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Zhonghe year one, Weibo forces attacked Heyang, routed Shuang at Xiuwu, and drove him from the city.

sentences.zh: 簡令大將守河陽。

translations.literal: Jian ordered a great general to garrison Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jian left a senior general to hold Heyang.

sentences.zh: 乃出師討曹全晸於鄆州。

translations.literal: He then sent out troops to campaign against Cao Quanzhen at Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched against Cao Quanzhen in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，孟州人復誘爽，爽自金商率兵千人，復入河陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the people of Meng Prefecture again enticed Shuang; Shuang from Jinsang led one thousand troops and again entered Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month men of Mengzhou lured Shuang back; he led a thousand troops from the Jin-Shang route and reoccupied Heyang.

sentences.zh: 乃犒勞魏人，令趙文㺹率之而去。

translations.literal: He then rewarded and comforted the Weibo men and ordered Zhao Wenwan to lead them away.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted the Weibo troops, then sent Zhao Wenwan to lead them home.

sentences.zh: 十一月，爽攻新鄉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Shuang attacked Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhuge Shuang attacked Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 簡自鄆來逆戰，軍於獲嘉西北。

translations.literal: Jian from Yan came to meet him in battle and encamped northwest of Huojia.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian marched from Yanzhou to oppose him and camped northwest of Huojia.

sentences.zh: 時簡將引魏人入趨關輔，誅除巢孽，自有圖王之誌，三軍屢諫不從。

translations.literal: At that time Jian intended to lead the Weibo men inward to hurry toward Guanfu, execute and remove Chao's brood, and had his own ambition to map out kingship; the three armies repeatedly remonstrated and he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jian meant to march the Weibo army west toward the capital to destroy Huang Chao's remnants and had begun to dream of kingship; his officers pleaded with him repeatedly, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 偏將樂彥禎因眾心搖，說激之，牙軍奔歸魏州。

translations.literal: The lateral general Le Yanfzhen, because popular hearts were swaying, spoke and stirred them, and the teeth-army fled back to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy commander Le Yanfzhen played on the troops' wavering loyalty until the elite guard deserted for Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 爽軍乘之。

translations.literal: Shuang's army took advantage of it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Shuang's forces pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 簡鄉兵八萬大敗，奔騰亂死，清水為之不流。

translations.literal: Jian's native troops eighty thousand were greatly defeated; they ran and surged in disorder and death, and the Clear Water for this did not flow.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian's eighty thousand levies were shattered; the rout was so deadly that the Qing River ran clogged with corpses.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，簡為牙軍所殺，爽軍由是大振。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year Jian was killed by the teeth-army, and Shuang's army from this was greatly invigorated.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month the guard murdered Han Jian, and Zhuge Shuang's command rose sharply in fortune.

sentences.zh: 及巢賊將敗，爽復歸國。

translations.literal: When Chao's bandits were about to be defeated, Shuang again returned to the state.
translations.idiomatic: As Huang Chao's rebellion collapsed, Shuang submitted to the Tang once more.

sentences.zh: 爽雖起群盜，既貴之後，善於為理；

translations.literal: Although Shuang rose from the mass of bandits, after he had been ennobled he was skilled at carrying out governance;
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhuge Shuang had risen from the outlaw ranks, once he held power he governed well;

sentences.zh: 所至法令澄清，人無怨嘆，人士以此多之。

translations.literal: Wherever he arrived the laws and orders were clear and pure, men had no resentful sighs, and scholars and gentry for this praised him much.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served the law was clear and complaints were rare, which won him praise from the gentry.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年，爽卒，帳中將劉經、張言以爽子仲方為孟帥。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangqi Shuang died; the tent generals Liu Jing and Zhang Yan made Shuang's son Zhongfang the Meng commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangqi year two he died; his staff officers Liu Jing and Zhang Yan installed his son Zhongfang as commander of Mengzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄而蔡賊孫儒率眾攻之，城陷於賊，仲方歸於汴，儒遂據孟州。

translations.literal: Before long the Cai bandit Sun Ru led the masses to attack him; the city fell to the bandits, Zhongfang returned to Bian, and Ru then occupied Meng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebel Sun Ru besieged the city, took it, and drove Zhongfang back to Bianzhou while Ru seized Mengzhou for himself.

sentences.zh: 高駢

translations.literal: =Gao Pian=
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian

sentences.zh: 高駢，字千里，幽州人。

translations.literal: Gao Pian, style name Qianli, was a man of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian, courtesy name Qianli, was a native of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖崇文，元和初功臣，封南平王，自有傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chongwen was an early Yuanhe merit-worthy, enfeoffed as King of Nanping, and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gao Chongwen, a founding hero of the Yuanhe reign, was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 父承明，神策虞候。

translations.literal: His father Chengming was a Shence chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gao Chengming had been a chief adjutant of the Shence armies.

sentences.zh: 駢，家世仕禁軍，幼而朗拔，好為文，多與儒者遊；

translations.literal: Pian's family for generations served the forbidden army; in youth he was bright and eminent, fond of composing literature, and much associated with Ruist scholars;
translations.idiomatic: Pian came from a family of imperial guardsmen; even as a youth he was brilliant, loved letters, and kept company with scholars;

sentences.zh: 喜言理道。

translations.literal: He delighted in speaking of principle and the Way.
translations.idiomatic: and liked to discourse on moral principle.

sentences.zh: 兩軍中貴，翕然稱重，乃縻之勇爵，累歷神策都虞候。

translations.literal: The noble eunuchs of the two armies all at once acclaimed and esteemed him, then tied him to a bravery peerage, and he repeatedly passed through Shence chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuchs admired him and fastened him to a military rank, until he rose through the posts of Shence chief adjutant.

sentences.zh: 會黨項羌叛，令率禁兵萬人戍長武城。

translations.literal: When the Tangut and Qiang rebelled, he was ordered to lead ten thousand forbidden troops to garrison Changwu Fort.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut and Qiang tribes revolted, he was ordered to lead ten thousand guardsmen to garrison Changwu.

sentences.zh: 時諸將禦羌無功，唯駢伺隙用兵，出無不捷。

translations.literal: At that time the various generals in resisting the Qiang had no achievement; only Pian watched for gaps to employ troops, and going forth there was none not victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Other generals could not check the Qiang, but Pian seized every opening and never marched without victory.

sentences.zh: 懿宗深嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yizong deeply praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 西蕃寇邊，移鎮秦州，尋授秦州刺史、本州經略使。

translations.literal: The western Tibetans harried the border; he was shifted to command Qin Prefecture, and soon was invested as prefect of Qin and native-prefecture frontier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans raided the frontier he was transferred to Qinzhou and soon made its prefect and military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先是，李琢為安南都護，貪於貨賄，虐賦夷獠，人多怨叛；

translations.literal: Before this, Li Zhuo was protector of Annan, greedy for goods and bribes, cruel in levying on the Yi and Liao, and many men resentfully rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Zhuo, as protector-general of Annan, had taken bribes and cruelly taxed the tribal peoples until many rose in revolt;

sentences.zh: 遂結蠻軍合勢攻安南，陷之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they joined the Man armies in combined momentum to attack Annan and overran it.
translations.idiomatic: They then united with tribal forces, overran Annan, and took the protectorate.

sentences.zh: 自是累年亟命將帥，未能收復。

translations.literal: From this for many years they repeatedly ordered generals and commanders, yet could not recover it.
translations.idiomatic: For years the court sent generals after generals but could not recover the territory.

sentences.zh: 五年，移駢為安南都護。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was shifted, with Pian as protector of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Gao Pian was appointed protector-general of Annan.

sentences.zh: 至則匡合五管之兵，期年之內，招懷溪洞，誅其首惡，一戰而蠻卒遁去，收復交州郡邑。

translations.literal: When he arrived he righted and united the troops of the five circuits; within the cycle of a year he recruited and embraced the stream caves, executed their chief evildoers, and in one battle the Man soldiers fled away and he recovered the commanderies and districts of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he assembled forces from all five southern circuits; within a year he won over the hill tribes, executed their ringleaders, routed the rebels in a single battle, and restored Jiaozhou and its dependencies.

sentences.zh: 又以廣州饋運艱澀，駢視其水路，自交至廣，多有巨石梗途，乃購募工徒，作法去之。

translations.literal: Also because Guangzhou's provision transport was arduous and obstructed, Pian surveyed its water route from Jiao to Guang; there were many huge stones blocking the way, so he purchased and recruited craftsmen and laborers and used methods to remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Because supply convoys from Guangzhou were chronically blocked, he surveyed the water route from Jiaozhi to Guangzhou, hired workers to blast the boulders that choked the channel, and cleared it.

sentences.zh: 由是舟楫無滯，安南儲備不乏，至今賴之。

translations.literal: From this boats and oars had no obstruction, Annan's stores were not wanting, and down to today they rely on it.
translations.idiomatic: Shipping moved freely thereafter, Annan's granaries stayed full, and the route still served the region.

sentences.zh: 天子嘉其才，遷檢校工部尚書、鄆州刺史、天平軍節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven praised his talent and transferred him to acting minister of works, prefect of Yan, commissioner of the Tianping army circuit and observation, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded his ability with acting minister of works, the governorship of Yanzhou, and command of the Tianping circuit.

sentences.zh: 治鄆之政，民吏歌之。

translations.literal: In governing Yan's administration, the people and clerks sang of him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule at Yanzhou won praise from officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 南詔蠻寇巂州，渡滬肆掠。

translations.literal: Nanzhao's Man raided Xi Prefecture, crossed the Lu and wantonly plundered.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanzhao attacked Xizhou and crossed the Lu River to raid unchecked,

sentences.zh: 乃以駢為成都尹、劍南西川節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: he was then made Pian metropolitan magistrate of Chengdu, commissioner of the Sword-South West circuit observation, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: Pian was made metropolitan governor of Chengdu and military governor of western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 蜀土散惡，成都比無垣墉，駢乃計每歲完葺之費，甃之以磚甓。

translations.literal: Shu lands were scattered and chancy; Chengdu compared to having no rampart walls; Pian then calculated the yearly costs of complete repair and paved them with brick and tile.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan was unstable and Chengdu had barely any walls; he budgeted annual repairs and faced them in brick.

sentences.zh: 雉堞由是完堅。

translations.literal: The battlements and crenels from this were complete and firm.
translations.idiomatic: The fortifications became solid and complete.

sentences.zh: 傳檄雲南，以兵壓境，講信修好，不敢入寇。

translations.literal: He transmitted a written order to Yunnan, pressed the border with troops, spoke faith and mended good relations, and they did not dare enter to harry.
translations.idiomatic: He sent dispatches to Yunnan backed by troops on the frontier, negotiated peace, and kept the kingdom from invading again.

sentences.zh: 進位檢校尚書右僕射、江陵尹、荊南節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: He advanced in rank to acting right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, metropolitan magistrate of Jiangling, commissioner of the Jingnan circuit observation, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, governor of Jiangling, and commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 乾符四年，進位檢校司空、潤州刺史、鎮海軍節度、浙江西道觀察等使，進封燕國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianfu he advanced to acting grand tutor, prefect of Run, military commissioner of the Zhenhai army and observer of the Zhejiang West circuit, and so on, and was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfu year four he rose to acting grand tutor, took Runzhou and command of the Zhenhai army and Zhexi circuit, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 時草賊王仙芝陷荊襄，宋威率諸道師討逐，其眾離散過江表。

translations.literal: At that time the grass-bandit Wang Xianzhi overran Jing and Xiang; Song Wei led the armies of the various circuits to pursue and expel them, and their masses scattered and crossed south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Wang Xianzhi seized Jingxiang, Song Wei drove him south until his followers scattered across the lower Yangtze region.

sentences.zh: 天子以駢前鎮鄆，軍民畏服，仙芝徒黨，鄆人也，故授駢京口節鉞，以招懷之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven because Pian had earlier commanded Yan, and the army and people feared and submitted, and Xianzhi's faction-followers were men of Yan, therefore invested Pian with the Jingkou seal and axe to recruit and embrace them.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew Pian had ruled Yanzhou to general satisfaction and that many of Xianzhi's followers were Yan natives, so it gave him the seal of command at Jingkou to win them over.

sentences.zh: 尋授諸道兵馬都統、江淮鹽鐵轉運等使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made overall commander of the armies of the various circuits and commissioner of Jiang-Huai salt and iron transport, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named overall military commander of all circuits and commissioner for Jiang-Huai salt and transport.

sentences.zh: 駢令其將張璘、梁纘分兵討賊，前後累捷，降其首領數十人。

translations.literal: Pian ordered his generals Zhang Lin and Liang Zuan to divide troops to campaign against the bandits; before and after they piled up victories and made surrender the chiefs and leaders, several tens of men.
translations.idiomatic: Pian sent Zhang Lin and Liang Zuan against the rebels; their repeated victories brought several dozen rebel chiefs to surrender.

sentences.zh: 賊南趨嶺表，天子嘉之。

translations.literal: The bandits hurried south toward Lingbiao; the Son of Heaven praised him.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels fled into Lingnan the emperor praised his service.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，進位檢校司徒、楊州大都督府長史、淮南節度副大使知節度事，兵馬都統、鹽鐵轉運使如故。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year he advanced to acting minister mentor, senior administrator of Yangzhou metropolitan prefecture, deputy military commissioner of Huainan knowing circuit affairs, with overall army commander and salt-and-iron transport commissioner as before.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was made acting minister mentor, chief administrator of Yangzhou, acting military governor of Huainan, while retaining his command of all forces and salt transport.

sentences.zh: 駢至淮南，繕完城壘，招募軍旅，土客之軍七萬。

translations.literal: When Pian reached Huainan he repaired and completed walls and ramparts, recruited armies and brigades, and had native and guest armies of seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At Huainan he rebuilt the walls, recruited troops, and raised seventy thousand men.

sentences.zh: 乃傳檄征天下兵，威望大振。

translations.literal: He then transmitted written orders to levy troops under Heaven; his awe-inspiring power greatly swelled.
translations.idiomatic: He issued calls for troops from across the empire and his prestige soared.

sentences.zh: 朝廷深倚賴之，進位檢校太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: The court deeply relied on him and advanced him to acting grand preceptor and co-serving as a chief steward of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The court leaned heavily upon him and promoted him to acting grand preceptor and chancellor.

sentences.zh: 既而黃巢賊合仙芝殘黨，復陷湖南、浙西州郡，眾號百萬。

translations.literal: Before long Huang Chao's bandits joined Xianzhi's remnant faction, again overran Hunan and the Zhexi prefectures and districts, and their masses were called a million.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huang Chao united Wang Xianzhi's remnants, retook Hunan and Zhexi, and his forces were said to number a million.

sentences.zh: 巢據廣州，求天平節鉞。

translations.literal: Chao held Guangzhou and requested the Tianping seal and axe.
translations.idiomatic: Chao held Guangzhou and demanded the Tianping command.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議欲以南海節鉞授之。

translations.literal: The court discussed intending to invest him with the Nanhai seal and axe.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated granting him the Nanhai governorship.

sentences.zh: 宰相盧攜與駢素善，以駢前在浙西已立討賊之效，今方集諸道之師於淮甸，不宜舍賊，以弱士心。

translations.literal: The chief steward Lu Xie and Pian had long been on good terms; because Pian earlier in Zhexi had already established the effect of campaigning against bandits, and now was just gathering the armies of the circuits at Huai fields, it was not fitting to abandon the bandits and thereby weaken soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Lu Xie, Pian's ally, argued that Pian had already proven himself against rebels in Zhexi and was now assembling armies on the Huai—abandoning the campaign would crush morale.

sentences.zh: 鄭畋議且宜假賊方鎮以紓難。

translations.literal: Zheng Tian discussed that for the moment it was fitting to lend the bandits a frontier command to ease distress.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tian urged temporarily granting Chao a frontier post to buy relief.

sentences.zh: 二人爭論於朝，以言詞不遜，由是兩罷之。

translations.literal: The two men disputed in court; because their words were not deferential, from this both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Their quarrel in court grew so heated that both were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 駢方持兵柄，聞朝議異同，心頗不平之。

translations.literal: Pian was just then holding the army's handle; hearing the court's discussions differed and agreed, in heart he was rather displeased with it.
translations.idiomatic: Pian, still holding military authority, took bitter exception to the divided court.

sentences.zh: 廣明元年夏，黃巢之黨自嶺表北趨江淮，由采石渡江。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Guangming Huang Chao's faction from Lingbiao north hurried toward Jiang-Huai and crossed the river by Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Guangming year one Huang Chao's followers marched north from Lingnan toward the Huai and crossed at Caishi.

sentences.zh: 張璘勒兵天長，欲擊之。

translations.literal: Zhang Lin drew up troops at Tianchang and wished to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin massed his troops at Tianchang to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 駢怨朝議有不附己者，欲賊縱橫河洛，令朝廷聳振，則從而誅之。

translations.literal: Pian resented that in court discussion some did not attach to him; he wished the bandits to run riot through He-Luo, to make the court start and shake, and then follow and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Angry that the court had sidelined him, he hoped to let the rebels ravage the north until the throne panicked and summoned him to deliver the killing blow.

sentences.zh: 大將畢師鐸曰：「妖賊百萬，所經鎮戍若蹈無人之境。

translations.literal: The great general Bi Shiduo said: "The demonic bandits are a million; wherever they pass the garrison commands are as if treading a land with no men.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Shiduo said, "A million rebels are sweeping through garrisons as though no one defended them.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷所恃者都統，破賊要害之地，唯江淮為首。

translations.literal: Now what the court relies on is the overall commander; the crucial ground for breaking the bandits—only Jiang-Huai is foremost.
translations.idiomatic: The throne's hope is you, Commander-in-Chief—and the Huai region is the decisive ground.

sentences.zh: 彼眾我寡，若不據津要以擊之，俾北渡長淮，何以扼束？

translations.literal: They are many and we few; if we do not hold the ford passes to strike them and let them north cross the Long Huai, how shall we throttle and bind them?
translations.idiomatic: They outnumber us; if we do not hold the crossings and strike now, once they cross the Huai how can we stop them?

sentences.zh: 中原陷覆必矣！」

translations.literal: The central plains' fall and ruin are certain!"
translations.idiomatic: The heartland will fall for certain!"

sentences.zh: 駢駭然曰：「君言是也。」

translations.literal: Pian startled said: "Your words are right."
translations.idiomatic: Pian started and said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 即令出軍。

translations.literal: He then ordered troops out.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the army forward.

sentences.zh: 有愛將呂用之者，以左道媚駢，駢頗用其言。

translations.literal: There was a cherished general Lu Yongzhi who, by heterodox ways, flattered Pian; Pian quite used his words.
translations.idiomatic: His favorite Lu Yongzhi had won his ear with occult arts, and Pian often heeded him.

sentences.zh: 用之懼師鐸等立功，即奪己權，從容謂駢曰：「相公勛業高矣，妖賊未殄，朝廷已有間言。

translations.literal: Yongzhi feared Bi Shiduo and others would achieve merit and at once seize his own power; at leisure he said to Pian: "Lord Chancellor, your meritorious work is already high; the demonic bandits are not yet exterminated, yet the court already has words of division.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi, fearing Bi Shiduo's glory would eclipse him, told Pian gently, "Your achievements are already towering, the rebels are not yet destroyed, and the court already whispers against you.

sentences.zh: 賊若蕩平，則威望震主，功居不賞，公安稅駕耶？

translations.literal: If the bandits are swept smooth, then your awe-inspiring power will shake the ruler; merit that has no reward—can the duke peacefully end his carriage?
translations.idiomatic: If you annihilate them, your fame will outshine the throne and unwelcome rewards will follow—will you retire in safety?

sentences.zh: 為公良畫，莫若觀釁，自求多福。」

translations.literal: For the duke's good planning, nothing is better than watching the crack and seeking much fortune for oneself."
translations.idiomatic: The wise course is to watch how the crisis unfolds and secure your own advantage."

sentences.zh: 駢深然之，乃止諸將，但握兵保境而已。

translations.literal: Pian deeply approved this; he then stopped the various generals and only held troops and guarded the border—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Pian agreed wholeheartedly, halted his generals, and merely held his troops within his borders.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，賊陷河洛。

translations.literal: That winter the bandits overran He-Luo.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the rebels took the Luoyang region.

sentences.zh: 中使促駢討賊，冠蓋相望。

translations.literal: Palace envoys urged Pian to campaign against the bandits; caps and carriages gazed at one another in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial envoys pressed him to march; they arrived in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 駢終逗撓不行。

translations.literal: Pian in the end dallied and stalled and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Pian stalled and never moved.

sentences.zh: 既而兩京覆沒，盧攜死。

translations.literal: Before long the two capitals were overturned and sunk; Lu Xie died.
translations.idiomatic: When both capitals fell Lu Xie died as well.

sentences.zh: 駢大閱軍師，欲兼並兩浙，為孫策三分之計。

translations.literal: Pian greatly reviewed his army and teachers, wished to swallow and merge the two Zhe circuits, and made a plan like Sun Ce's tripartite division.
