translations.idiomatic: He held a grand review and plotted to annex the two Zhe circuits in a scheme modeled on Sun Ce's partition of the realm.

sentences.zh: 天子在蜀，亟命出師。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was in Shu and urgently ordered troops out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, exiled in Shu, repeatedly ordered him to march.

sentences.zh: 中和二年五月，雉雊於揚州廨舍，占者云：「野鳥入室，軍府將空。」

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Zhonghe, pheasants crowed in the Yangzhou government offices; the diviner said: "Wild birds enter the chamber—the military government will be emptied."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Zhonghe year two a pheasant crowed in the Yangzhou offices; diviners said, "Wild birds indoors mean the command will be emptied."

sentences.zh: 駢心惡之。

translations.literal: Pian in heart hated this.
translations.idiomatic: Pian was deeply unsettled.

sentences.zh: 其月，盡出兵於東塘，結壘而處，每日教閱，如赴難之勢。

translations.literal: That month he wholly sent out troops to Dongtang, built ramparts and dwelled there, daily drilled and reviewed, like the momentum of hurrying to distress.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he moved his entire force to Dongtang, built camps, and drilled daily as though racing to the capital's relief.

sentences.zh: 仍與浙西周寶書，請同入援京師。

translations.literal: Still he wrote Zhou Bao of Zhexi, requesting together to enter and aid the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Zhou Bao of western Zhejiang proposing a joint march to save the capital.

sentences.zh: 寶大喜，即點閱，將赴之，遣人偵之，知其非實。

translations.literal: Bao was greatly pleased, at once mustered and reviewed, and was about to go; he sent men to spy on it and knew it was not real.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bao rejoiced, mustered his troops to join him, then sent scouts and learned the offer was a sham.

sentences.zh: 駢在東塘凡百日，復還廣陵，蓋禳雊雉之異也。

translations.literal: Pian at Dongtang altogether a hundred days, then returned to Guangling—it was broadly to exorcise the omen of the crowing pheasant.
translations.idiomatic: After a hundred days at Dongtang he returned to Guangling, performing rites to dispel the omen of the crowing pheasant.

sentences.zh: 僖宗知駢無赴難意，乃以宰臣王鐸為京城四面諸道行營兵馬都統，崔安潛副之，韋昭度領江淮鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong knew Pian had no mind to hurry to distress; he then made chief steward Wang Duo overall commander of the encampment armies of the four sides of the capital city from the various circuits, with Cui Anqian as deputy, and Wei Zhaodu heading Jiang-Huai salt-and-iron transport.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Pian would not rescue the throne, Emperor Xizong named Wang Duo supreme commander around the capital, Cui Anqian as his deputy, and Wei Zhaodu over Jiang-Huai salt and transport.

sentences.zh: 增駢階爵，使務並停。

translations.literal: He increased Pian's grade and peerage, and let his commissions all stop together.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Pian's titles but stripped him of every commission at once.

sentences.zh: 駢既失兵柄，又落利權，攘袂大詬，累上章論列，語詞不遜。

translations.literal: Pian had already lost the army's handle and again fell from profit's power; he waved his sleeves and greatly cursed, repeatedly submitted memorials arguing and ranking, and his words were not deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of military and fiscal power, Pian raged and sent memorial after memorial in insubordinate language.

sentences.zh: 其末章曰：臣伏奉詔命，令臣自省，更勿依違者。

translations.literal: Its last section said: Your servant humbly received the imperial order commanding me to examine myself and no longer to defy or disobey.
translations.idiomatic: The final section read: Your servant has received the edict ordering self-examination and strict compliance hereafter.

sentences.zh: 臣仰天訴地，自淚交流；

translations.literal: Your servant looked up to heaven and complained to earth; tears by themselves streamed down.
translations.idiomatic: I lift my eyes to heaven and pour out my grief to earth; tears flow unchecked.

sentences.zh: 如劍戟攢心，若湯火在己。

translations.literal: It is as if swords and halberds pierce the heart, as if boiling water and fire were in one's own body.
translations.idiomatic: My heart feels pierced by blades; I burn as though scalded by fire.

sentences.zh: 只如黃巢大寇，圍逼天長小城，四旬有余，竟至敗走。

translations.literal: Take for example the great bandit Huang Chao: he besieged and pressed the small city of Tianchang for more than forty days and in the end was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Huang Chao's great rebellion: his siege of Tianchang lasted over forty days before he was driven off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 臣散征諸道兵甲，盡出家財賞給，而諸道多不發兵，財物即為己有。

translations.literal: Your servant dispersed summons to the various circuits for armor and troops and exhausted the family wealth to bestow rewards, yet most circuits did not send troops and kept the goods for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: I levied troops from every circuit and spent my own fortune on pay, yet most commands refused to send men and kept the money themselves.

sentences.zh: 縱然遣使征得，敕旨不許過淮。

translations.literal: Even if envoys were sent and goods were obtained, the imperial decree did not permit crossing south of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Even when envoys secured supplies, the throne forbade them to cross the Huai River.

sentences.zh: 其時黃巢殘兇，才及二萬，經過數千里，軍鎮盡若無人。

translations.literal: At that time Huang Chao's remnants were cruel; they amounted to only twenty thousand, yet after passing several thousand li, military posts were all as if without a single man.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao's battered force numbered barely twenty thousand, yet for thousands of li every garrison seemed deserted.

sentences.zh: 只如潼關已東，止有一徑，其為險固，甚於井陘。

translations.literal: Take Tong Pass eastward: there is only one route; its strategic strength is greater than that of Jingxing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: East of Tong Pass there is but one narrow road, more defensible even than Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 豈有狂寇奔沖，略無阻礙，即百二之地，固是虛言。

translations.literal: How could a mad bandit charge and rush with scarcely any obstruction—that the land of one hundred and two strongholds is in truth empty talk?
translations.idiomatic: How could a reckless raider sweep through unopposed? The boast of impregnable terrain was plainly false.

sentences.zh: 神策六軍，此時安在？

translations.literal: The six armies of the Shence Corps—where were they at this time?
translations.idiomatic: Where were the six Shence armies when this happened?

sentences.zh: 陛下蒼黃西出，內官奔命東來，黎庶盡被殺傷，衣冠悉遭屠戮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty fled west in panic; eunuch officials rushed east on urgent orders; common folk were entirely killed and wounded; officials and gentry were all butchered.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty fled west in haste while palace eunuchs raced east; civilians were slaughtered and the scholar-official class massacred.

sentences.zh: 今則園陵開毀，宗廟荊榛，遠近痛傷，遐邇嗟怨。

translations.literal: Now imperial tombs have been opened and destroyed, ancestral temples overgrown with brambles; near and far are grieved and wounded, in every quarter there are sighs of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Royal tombs lie desecrated and ancestral halls choked with weeds; grief and anger resound everywhere.

sentences.zh: 雖然，奸臣未悟，陛下猶迷，不思宗廟之焚燒，不痛園陵之開毀。

translations.literal: Even so, treacherous ministers have not awakened; Your Majesty still wanders in delusion, not pondering the burning of the ancestral temples, not pained by the opening and destruction of the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet wicked ministers remain unawakened and Your Majesty unmoved, heedless of burned temples and desecrated tombs.

sentences.zh: 臣之痛也，實在於斯！

translations.literal: Your servant's pain truly lies in this!
translations.idiomatic: It is here that my anguish truly lies!

sentences.zh: 此事見之多年，不獨知於今日。

translations.literal: This matter has been seen for many years; I alone do not know it only today.
translations.idiomatic: This has been plain for years, not only revealed today.

sentences.zh: 況自萑蒲盜起，朝廷征用至多，上至帥臣，下及裨將，以臣所料，悉可坐擒，用此為謀，安能辦事？

translations.literal: Moreover, since the thieves of wild grass and rushes arose, the court has conscripted so many—from chief commanders above to adjutant generals below—that in your servant's estimate all could be taken while seated; using this as a plan, how can affairs be accomplished?
translations.idiomatic: Since the uprising began the court has conscripted commanders and junior officers alike—men I believe could be captured without effort—yet such a strategy can accomplish nothing.

sentences.zh: 陛下今用王鐸，盡主兵權，誠知狂寇必殲，梟巢即覆。

translations.literal: Your Majesty now employs Wang Duo, giving him full command over military power; truly knowing the mad bandits must be exterminated and the chief nest overthrown at once.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now puts Wang Duo in full command of the armies, evidently certain the rebels will be destroyed and their nest overturned.

sentences.zh: 臣讀《禮》至宣尼射於矍相之圃，蓋觀者如堵墻，使子路出延射曰：「潰軍之將，亡國之大夫，與為人後者，不入於射也。」

translations.literal: Your servant read the Rites to the passage where Confucius shot in the garden of Ju Xiang; the onlookers were like a wall; he had Zilu go out to extend the invitation to shoot, saying: "Generals of a routed army, grand masters of a perished state, and those who have become another's successor may not enter the archery ground."
translations.idiomatic: In the Rites I read of Confucius shooting at Ju Xiang's garden before a crowd packed like a wall, when he sent Zilu to announce: "Generals of a defeated army, ministers of a ruined state, and those who have become another man's heir shall not take part in the contest."

sentences.zh: 嚴誡如斯，圖功也，豈宜容易？

translations.literal: The strict admonition is like this; to seek achievement, how should it be easy?
translations.idiomatic: With such stern warning recorded, how lightly dare one expect success?

sentences.zh: 陛下安忍委敗軍之將，陷一儒臣？

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty bear to entrust a general of a defeated army and trap one scholar-official?
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty bear to commit a defeated general—and a mere scholar-official at that?

sentences.zh: 崔安潛到處貪殘，只如西川，可為驗矣，委之副貳，詎可平戎？

translations.literal: Cui Anqian is everywhere greedy and cruel; western Shu alone suffices as proof; to entrust him as deputy—how can he pacify the barbarians?
translations.idiomatic: Cui Anqian's greed and cruelty are proven in western Shu; how can such a man as deputy win the war?

sentences.zh: 況天下兵驕，在處僭越，豈二儒士，能戢強兵，萬一乖張，將何救助？

translations.literal: Moreover, throughout the realm soldiers are arrogant; everywhere they overstep bounds; could two Confucian scholars restrain powerful troops? If by chance things go awry, what rescue will there be?
translations.idiomatic: The armies are arrogant and lawless everywhere; can two scholars restrain them? If things go wrong, who will save us?

sentences.zh: 願陛下下念黎庶，上為宗祧，無使百代有抱恨之臣，千古留刮席之恥！

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty below to think on the common people and above on the imperial ancestral line, that no age after age should have a minister nursing resentment, and that for a thousand years no disgrace of scraping the mat be left!
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to care for the people below and the ancestral line above, lest future generations inherit embittered ministers and the shame of Liu Bo for a thousand years!

sentences.zh: 臣但慮寇生東土，劉氏復興，即軹道之災，豈獨往日！

translations.literal: Your servant only fears that bandits arise in the eastern lands, the Liu house revives—the disaster of Zhidao is not confined to days past alone!
translations.idiomatic: I fear only that rebels rise in the east and the Liu house revive; the disaster of Zhidao is not merely a story of the past!

sentences.zh: 乞陛下稍留神慮，以安宗社。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty slightly to keep attention and concern, to settle the altars of state and ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: I implore Your Majesty to ponder this carefully for the sake of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 今賢才在野，憸人滿朝，致陛下為亡國之君，此等計將安出？

translations.literal: Now worthy talent is in the wilds and slanderous men fill the court, so that Your Majesty becomes a ruler of a perished state—by what means shall such a plan be produced?
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men languish outside while flatterers fill the court, making Your Majesty a ruler in name of a dying dynasty—what counsel can remedy this?

sentences.zh: 伏乞戮賣官鬻爵之輩，征鯁直公正之臣，委之重難，置之左右，克復宮闕，莫尚於斯！

translations.literal: Your servant humbly begs to execute those who sell offices and peddle ranks, to summon upright and fair ministers, to entrust them with grave tasks and place them at Your side—there is nothing greater than this for recovering the palace halls!
translations.idiomatic: Execute those who sell offices, summon upright ministers, place them at Your side in command of the crisis—nothing avails more to recover the capital!

sentences.zh: 若此時謗誹忠臣，沈埋烈士，匡復宗社，未見有期！

translations.literal: If at this time loyal ministers are slandered and heroic martyrs are buried and suppressed, restoring the altars of state—no time is yet seen!
translations.idiomatic: If loyal ministers are slandered and heroes silenced now, restoration of the dynasty will never come.

sentences.zh: 臣受國恩深，不覺語切，無任憂懼之至。

translations.literal: Your servant has received the state's grace deeply and without knowing it spoke urgently; I cannot bear the utmost of worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply indebted to the state, I have spoken bluntly from overwhelming dread.

sentences.zh: 詔報駢曰：省表具悉。

translations.literal: An edict in reply to Pian said: I have read your memorial and understand it all.
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied to Pian: Your memorial has been received and reviewed in full.

sentences.zh: 卿一門忠孝，三代勛庸，銘於景鐘，煥在青史。

translations.literal: Your clan in one gate has loyalty and filial piety; for three generations there has been meritorious service—inscribed on the bell of Jing, shining in the blue annals.
translations.idiomatic: Your house is famed for loyalty across three generations, recorded on the bell of Jing and bright in history.

sentences.zh: 卿承祖父之訓，襲弓冶之基，起自禁軍，從微至著。

translations.literal: You inherited your grandfather and father's instruction, took up the foundation of bow-casting and smelting, rose from the palace armies, from the lowly to the conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: You followed your forebears' teaching, rose from the palace guard from obscurity to renown.

sentences.zh: 始則囊錐露穎，稍有知音；

translations.literal: At first, like an awl in a pouch exposing its point, you gradually had those who knew your sound;
translations.idiomatic: At first your talent broke through like an awl from a bag and found a few who recognized it;

sentences.zh: 尋則天驥呈才，急於試效。

translations.literal: Soon a heavenly steed displayed talent, eager to prove its effect.
translations.idiomatic: Soon you showed the ability of a heavenly steed, eager to prove yourself in service.

sentences.zh: 自秦州經略使，授交趾節旄，聯翩寵榮，汗漫富貴，未嘗斷絕，僅二十年。

translations.literal: From Qinzhou frontier commissioner, conferred the command batons of Jiaozhi—successive waves of favor and glory, boundless wealth and honor—never once broken off, barely twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: From frontier commissioner at Qinzhou to commander of Jiaozhi, honors and wealth piled upon you without break for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 卿報國之功，亦可悉數。

translations.literal: Your achievements in repaying the state can also be counted one by one.
translations.idiomatic: Your services to the state can be counted in detail.

sentences.zh: 最顯赫者，安南拒蠻，至今海隅尚守。

translations.literal: Most illustrious is repelling the barbarians in Annam; to this day the sea's edge is still guarded.
translations.idiomatic: Foremost is your defense of Annam against the tribes; the southern coast remains secure to this day.

sentences.zh: 次則汶陽之日，政聲洽平。

translations.literal: Next, in the days at Wenyang, your governing reputation was harmonious and peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: Next came your tenure at Wenyang, where your governance won universal praise.

sentences.zh: 洎臨成都，脅歸驃信，三載之內，亦無侵淩。

translations.literal: When you arrived at Chengdu, you compelled the return of Biao Xin; within three years there was likewise no invasion or oppression.
translations.idiomatic: At Chengdu you compelled the submission of Biao Xin, and for three years there was no further raid.

sentences.zh: 創築羅城，大新錦裏，其為雄壯，實少比儔。

translations.literal: You newly built the outer city and greatly renewed Jinli; its majesty and strength truly had few equals.
translations.idiomatic: You built the outer wall and renewed Jinli—works of grandeur seldom matched.

sentences.zh: 渚宮不暇於施為，便當移鎮；

translations.literal: At Zhugong you had no leisure for action and should have moved your command;
translations.idiomatic: You barely began work at Zhugong before you were transferred;

sentences.zh: 建鄴才聞於安靜，旋即渡江。

translations.literal: At Jiankang the realm had just heard of quiet order, and you immediately crossed the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Scarcely had Jiankang learned of peace when you crossed the Yangzi again.

sentences.zh: 自到廣陵，並鐘多壘，即亦招降草寇，救援臨淮。

translations.literal: Since arriving at Guangling, you combined the bells and many ramparts, and also summoned surrender from grass bandits and rescued Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangling you fortified the defenses, accepted rebel surrenders, and relieved Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 大約昭灼功勛，不大於此數者。

translations.literal: Generally speaking, your bright and manifest accomplishments are not greater in number than these.
translations.idiomatic: In sum, your notable achievements are no more than these.

sentences.zh: 朝廷累加渥澤，靡吝徽章，位極三公，兵環大鎮。

translations.literal: The court repeatedly added thick favor, sparing no insignia of rank; your position reached the three dukes, and armies surrounded the great command.
translations.idiomatic: The court heaped honors upon you to the rank of Grand Preceptor, with armies under command at a great post.

sentences.zh: 銅鹽重務，綰握約及七年；

translations.literal: The weighty duties of copper and salt you grasped in hand for about seven years;
translations.idiomatic: You held the lucrative salt monopoly for some seven years;

sentences.zh: 都統雄籓，幅圓幾於萬里。

translations.literal: As overall commander over a mighty frontier, the compass of authority approached ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: And as supreme commander your authority spanned nearly ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 朕瞻如太華，倚若長城，凡有奏論，無不依允，其為托賴，豈愧神明？

translations.literal: I looked to you as to Mount Taihua, relied on you as on the Long Wall; whatever memorials and arguments you made, none were not obeyed and granted—such trust and reliance, how would it shame the spirits?
translations.idiomatic: I looked to you as Mount Taihua and relied on you as the Long Wall; every petition of yours was granted—such trust would honor any ruler before heaven.

sentences.zh: 自黃巢肆毒鹹京，卿並不離隋苑。

translations.literal: Since Huang Chao spread poison through the salty capital, you did not leave the Sui garden.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment Huang Chao ravaged Chang'an you never left your Yangzhou palace grounds.

sentences.zh: 豈金陵苑水，能遮鵝鸛之雄；

translations.literal: Can the garden waters of Jinling block the might of geese and cranes?
translations.idiomatic: Could Yangzhou's ponds and parks block an army as mighty as marching geese and cranes?

sentences.zh: 風伯雨師，終阻帆檣之利？

translations.literal: Could the wind lord and rain master in the end obstruct the advantage of sails and masts?
translations.idiomatic: Could wind and rain forever keep your fleet from sailing?

sentences.zh: 自聞歸止，寧免郁陶。

translations.literal: Since hearing of your return and settling, how could I avoid dark distress?
translations.idiomatic: Since learning of your withdrawal, could I feel anything but anguish?

sentences.zh: 卿既安住蕪城，鄭畋以春初入覲，遂命上相，親領師徒，因落卿都統之名，固亦不乖事例。

translations.literal: Since you were securely settled in Wucheng, Zheng Tian came to audience at the beginning of spring; I then appointed the chief minister to lead the army in person, and by that removed your title of overall commander—this certainly does not deviate from precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When you were settled at Yangzhou and Zheng Tian came to court in spring, I named the chief minister to take command in person and removed your title of supreme commander—no breach of precedent.

sentences.zh: 仍加封實，貴表優恩。

translations.literal: I still added fief and solid reward, showing precious marks of gracious favor.
translations.idiomatic: I even added rewards and noble titles to show special favor.

sentences.zh: 何乃疑忿太深，指陳過當，移時省讀，深用震嗟。

translations.literal: Why then is suspicion and resentment so deep, your pointing out and stating so excessive? For a long while on reading it I was deeply shocked and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Why then such deep suspicion and such excessive accusations? Reading them at length, I am deeply dismayed.

sentences.zh: 聊舉諸條，粗申報復。

translations.literal: I briefly raise several items to give a rough reply in return.
translations.idiomatic: I will briefly answer point by point.

sentences.zh: 卿表云：「自是陛下不用微臣，固非微臣有負陛下」者。

translations.literal: Your memorial says: "From this it is Your Majesty who does not use your humble servant; it is certainly not that your humble servant has failed Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: You wrote: "It is Your Majesty who has ceased to employ me, not I who have failed Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 朕拔卿汶上，超領劍南，荊、潤、維、揚，聯居四鎮。

translations.literal: I raised you from Wen in Shandong, promoted you to lead Jiannan; Jing, Run, Wei, Yang—you held four commands in succession.
translations.idiomatic: I raised you from Shandong to command Jiannan and successively Jing, Run, Wei, and Yang—four great circuits.

sentences.zh: 綰利則牢盆在手，主兵則都統當權。

translations.literal: When grasping profit, the salt monopoly was in hand; when commanding troops, the overall commander held power.
translations.idiomatic: You held the salt monopoly in your grip and supreme military authority in your hands.

sentences.zh: 直至京北、京南、神策諸鎮，悉在指揮之下，可知董制之雄。

translations.literal: Right up to the northern capital, southern capital, and Shence commands—all were under your direction; one may know the might of your sole control.
translations.idiomatic: Even the garrisons north and south of the capital and the Shence armies were under your command—such was your dominance.

sentences.zh: 而乃貴作司徒，榮為太尉，以為不用，何名為用乎？

translations.literal: And yet you were honored as Minister over the Masses and glorified as Grand Commandant—if this is called not being used, what is called being used?
translations.idiomatic: You were made Minister over the Masses and Grand Commandant—if that is not being used, what would be?

sentences.zh: 卿又云：「若欲俯念舊勛，佇觀後效，何不以王鐸權位，與臣主持，必能糾率諸侯，誅鋤群盜」者。

translations.literal: You also said: "If you wish to look down in consideration of old merit and wait to observe later effect, why not give Wang Duo's power and rank to your servant to take charge—surely able to discipline and lead the lords, execute and root out all bandits."
translations.idiomatic: You also wrote: "If you wish to honor past service and await future results, why not give Wang Duo's rank and authority to me? I would surely rally the lords and exterminate the rebels."

sentences.zh: 朕緣久付卿兵柄，不能翦滅元兇。

translations.literal: I because I long entrusted you with the army's handle could not cut down and destroy the chief villain.
translations.idiomatic: Because I long entrusted you with military power, the chief rebel was never destroyed.

sentences.zh: 自天長漏網過淮，不出一兵襲逐，奄殘京國，首尾三年；

translations.literal: From Tianchang he slipped through the net and crossed the Huai; not a single soldier went out in pursuit; suddenly he ravaged the capital region—three years from start to finish;
translations.idiomatic: After he escaped Tianchang and crossed the Huai you sent not one soldier in pursuit; for three years he ravaged the heartland unchecked;

sentences.zh: 廣陵之師，未離封部，忠臣積望，勇士興譏。

translations.literal: The armies of Guangling never left their sealed circuit; loyal ministers piled up hopes; bold warriors rose in ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: While your Guangling armies never left your own territory—loyal ministers grew desperate and warriors mocked.

sentences.zh: 所以擢用元臣，誅夷巨寇，心期貔武，便掃欃槍。

translations.literal: Therefore I promoted and employed a chief minister, executed and destroyed the great bandit; in heart I expected fierce warriors and immediately to sweep away the comet banner.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I promoted a chief minister to destroy the great rebel, expecting brave warriors at once to sweep the traitors away.

sentences.zh: 卿初委張璘，請放卻諸道兵士，辛勤召置，容易放還，璘果敗亡，巢益顛越。

translations.literal: You at first entrusted Zhang Lin, requested release of the soldiers from the various circuits; after laboriously gathering and placing them, you easily let them return; Lin indeed failed and perished, and Chao grew more wildly unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: You first sent Zhang Lin, asked to dismiss the allied troops—after painstakingly assembling them you let them go; Lin was defeated and Chao grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 卿前年初夏，逞發神機，與京中朝貴書，題云：「得靈仙教導，芒種之後，賊必蕩平。」

translations.literal: In the early summer of the year before last you boldly sent divine schemes, writing to the court nobles in the capital, with the heading saying: "Having received the guidance of numinous immortals, after Grain in Ear the bandits will surely be swept away and pacified."
translations.idiomatic: In early summer two years ago you flaunted divine prophecies, writing to court nobles in the capital: "Guided by immortals, after Grain in Ear the rebels will be annihilated."

sentences.zh: 尋聞圍逼天長，必謂死在卿手，豈知魚跳鼎釜，狐脫網羅，遽過長淮，竟為大憝。

translations.literal: Soon hearing of the siege pressing Tianchang, surely one thought he would die in your hand; who would know a fish leaping from the cauldron, a fox slipping from the net—hastily crossing the Long Huai and in the end becoming the great enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When he besieged Tianchang you surely expected his end—but like a fish leaping from the pot and a fox from the net he suddenly crossed the Huai and became the direst threat of all.

sentences.zh: 都統既不能禦遏，諸將更何以枝梧？

translations.literal: The overall commander could neither obstruct nor restrain—what more could the generals use to prop up?
translations.idiomatic: If the supreme commander could not stop him, what could his generals do?

sentences.zh: 果致連犯關河，繼傾都邑。

translations.literal: It indeed caused successive violations of passes and rivers, and in turn the toppling of capitals.
translations.idiomatic: The result was successive breaches of frontier passes and the fall of capital cities.

sentences.zh: 從來倚仗之意，一旦控告無門，凝睇東南，惟增淒惻。

translations.literal: The trust on which I had always relied—in one morning there was no gate to plead my case; gazing fixedly toward the southeast, I only increased desolate sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The ally I had always counted on offered no recourse; gazing southeast, I could only feel deeper grief.

sentences.zh: 及朕蒙塵入蜀，宗廟汙於賊庭，天下人心，無不雪涕。

translations.literal: When I suffered dust and entered Shu, the ancestral temples were defiled in the bandits' court; the hearts of all under heaven—none did not weep tears like snow.
translations.idiomatic: When I fled into Shu and the ancestral temples were defiled in enemy hands, none under heaven failed to weep.

sentences.zh: 既知歷數猶在，謳謠未移，則懷忠拗怒之臣，貯救難除奸之誌，便須果決，安可因循？

translations.literal: Since I know the dynastic mandate still remains and songs of praise have not shifted, then ministers who hold loyalty and nursing anger, storing plans to save from distress and remove traitors—one must be resolute; how can one procrastinate?
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the mandate still holds and loyalty not wholly lost, ministers resolved on rescue must act decisively—how could one delay?

sentences.zh: 況恩厚者其報深，位重者其心急。

translations.literal: Moreover, those whose grace is deep should report deeply; those whose position is weighty should have urgent hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Those most favored owe the deepest duty; those highest in rank should feel the greatest urgency.

sentences.zh: 此際天下義舉，皆望淮海率先。

translations.literal: At this moment righteous undertakings throughout the realm all looked to Huai-Hai to take the lead.
translations.idiomatic: At this hour the whole empire looked to the Huai-Hai region to lead the loyal cause.

sentences.zh: 豈知近輔儒臣，先為首唱；

translations.literal: Who would know that a nearby assisting Confucian minister would first be the lead singer?
translations.idiomatic: Who expected a court scholar close at hand to be the first to complain?

sentences.zh: 而窮邊勇將，誓誌平戎，關東寂寥，不見幹羽。

translations.literal: While brave generals on the remote frontier swore resolve to pacify the barbarians, east of the passes was desolate—no sight of the shield and axes of peace.
translations.idiomatic: While frontier generals swore to pacify the rebels, the east lay silent—no sign of loyal arms.

sentences.zh: 洎乎初秋覽表，方雲仲夏發兵，便詔軍前，並移汶上。

translations.literal: When in early autumn I viewed your memorial, you had just said you would send troops in midsummer; I then ordered the army forward and also moved to Wen in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: When I read your memorial in early autumn you had just promised midsummer mobilization; I ordered the armies forward and moved you to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 喜聞兵勢，渴見旌幢。

translations.literal: I rejoiced to hear of the army's momentum and thirsted to see the banners and flags.
translations.idiomatic: I rejoiced at news of your forces and eagerly awaited your banners.

sentences.zh: 尋稱宣潤阻艱，難從天討。

translations.literal: Soon you said Xuan and Run were blocked and difficult, and hard to follow the Heavenly punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Soon you cited difficulties in Xuanzhou and Runzhou and declined the imperial punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 謝玄破苻堅於淝水，裴度平元濟於淮西，未必儒臣不如武將！

translations.literal: Xie Xuan broke Fu Jian at the Fei River; Pei Du pacified Wu Yuanji in Huai-Xi—Confucian ministers are not necessarily inferior to military generals!
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan routed Fu Jian at the Fei River and Pei Du crushed Wu Yuanji in Huai-Xi—scholars are not always lesser than generals!

sentences.zh: 卿又云：「若不斥逐邪佞，親近忠良，臣既不能保家，陛下豈能安國？

translations.literal: You also said: "If you do not drive away wicked flatterers and draw near to loyal and good men, your servant cannot preserve the family—can Your Majesty secure the state?
translations.idiomatic: You also wrote: "Unless wicked men are expelled and the loyal embraced, I cannot protect my house—can Your Majesty secure the realm?

sentences.zh: 忽當今日，棄若寒灰」者。

translations.literal: Suddenly faced with today, cast off like cold ashes."
translations.idiomatic: Yet today I am cast off like cold ashes."

sentences.zh: 未委誰是忠良，誰為邪佞？

translations.literal: I have not been informed who are loyal and good, and who are wicked flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: Who exactly are the loyal, and who the wicked?

sentences.zh: 終日寵榮富貴，何嘗不保其家；

translations.literal: All day favored, honored, wealthy and noble—when have you not preserved your family?
translations.idiomatic: You enjoy unceasing honors and wealth—when have you failed to protect your house?

sentences.zh: 無人扞禦冠戎，所以不安其國。

translations.literal: No one defended against the cap-wearing invaders—that is why the state is not secure.
translations.idiomatic: No one defended the realm against the invaders—that is why the state is not secure.

sentences.zh: 豈有位兼將相，使帶銅鹽，自謂寒灰，真同浪語。

translations.literal: How could one whose rank combines general and minister, commissioner over copper and salt, call himself cold ashes—truly the same as reckless talk.
translations.idiomatic: For one holding both civil and military power and the salt monopoly to call himself cold ashes is absurd.

sentences.zh: 卿又云：「不通園陵之開毀，不念宗廟之焚燒，臣實痛之，實在茲也。」

translations.literal: You also said: "Not understanding the opening and destruction of imperial tombs, not considering the burning of ancestral temples—your servant truly pains at this; it truly lies here."
translations.idiomatic: You also wrote: "Unaware of the desecration of tombs and the burning of temples—my pain lies precisely here."

sentences.zh: 且龜玉毀於櫝中，誰之過也？

translations.literal: Moreover, tortoise and jade are destroyed in the casket—whose fault is it?
translations.idiomatic: When the treasure is ruined in its case, whose fault is that?

sentences.zh: 鯨鯢漏於網外，抑有其由！

translations.literal: When whales and crocodiles slip outside the net, there is perhaps a reason!
translations.idiomatic: When the monster escapes the net, there is surely a reason!

sentences.zh: 卿手握強兵，身居大鎮，不能遮圍擒戮，致令脫漏猖狂，雖則上系天時，抑亦旁由人事。

translations.literal: You grasped strong troops in hand and personally occupied a great command; you could not obstruct, besiege, capture and kill, causing him to slip free and run wild—although above it may depend on Heaven's season, it also plainly arises from human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With a strong army and great command you failed to surround and capture him, allowing his escape and rampage—though Heaven may share the blame, human failure is plain.

sentences.zh: 朕自到西蜀，不離一室之中，屏棄笙歌，杜絕遊獵，蔬食適口，布服被身，焚香以望園陵，雪涕以思宗廟，省躬罪己，不敢遑安。

translations.literal: Since I arrived in western Shu I have not left a single chamber; I have set aside pipes and songs, cut off hunting, eaten vegetables to suit the mouth, worn cloth clothes on the body, burned incense to gaze toward the imperial tombs, wept tears like snow thinking on the ancestral temples, examined myself and blamed myself—I dare not leisurely rest.
translations.idiomatic: Since reaching western Shu I have scarcely left my chamber, rejected music and hunting, eaten plainly, dressed in coarse cloth, burned incense toward the tombs, wept for the temples, and blamed myself—I dare not rest easy.

sentences.zh: 「奸臣未悟」之言，誰人肯認？

translations.literal: The words "treacherous ministers have not awakened"—who would be willing to accept them?
translations.idiomatic: Who would accept your charge that "wicked ministers remain unawakened"?

sentences.zh: 「陛下猶迷」之語，朕不敢當！

translations.literal: The words "Your Majesty still wanders in delusion"—I dare not accept!
translations.idiomatic: Your claim that "I remain deluded" I dare not accept!

sentences.zh: 卿又云：「自來所用將帥，上至帥臣，下及裨將，以臣所料，悉可坐擒，用此為謀，安能集事」者。

translations.literal: You also said: "From past to present the generals and commanders employed—from chief commanders above to adjutant generals below—in your servant's estimate all could be taken while seated; using this as a plan, how can affairs be gathered and accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: You also wrote: "The generals the court has used, from commanders to adjutants—all could in my view be captured without effort; such planning can accomplish nothing."

sentences.zh: 且十室之邑，猶有忠信，天下至大，豈無英雄？

translations.literal: Moreover, in a settlement of ten houses there are still loyalty and good faith; the realm is vastly great—how could there be no heroes?
translations.idiomatic: Even a hamlet of ten houses holds the faithful; in so vast an empire, how could heroes be lacking?

sentences.zh: 況守固城池，悉嚴兵甲，縱非盡美，安得平欺？

translations.literal: Moreover they guard firm city walls and all strictly array armor and troops; even if not wholly perfect, how can one be freely deceived?
translations.idiomatic: They hold fortified cities under strict arms—even if not perfect, how can they be dismissed so lightly?

sentences.zh: 卿尚不能縛黃巢於天長，安能坐擒諸將？

translations.literal: You still cannot bind Huang Chao at Tianchang—how can you take the various generals while seated?
translations.idiomatic: You could not even hold Huang Chao at Tianchang—how can you casually capture every general?

sentences.zh: 只如拓拔思恭、諸葛爽輩，安能坐擒耶？

translations.literal: Take for example Tabgach Sigong, Zhuge Shuang and their sort—how could they be taken while seated?
translations.idiomatic: Take Tabgach Sigong and Zhuge Shuang—could they be captured without a fight?

sentences.zh: 勿務大言，不堪垂訓。

translations.literal: Do not pursue grand words; they cannot serve as instruction handed down.
translations.idiomatic: Do not indulge such grand talk—it is unworthy of counsel.

sentences.zh: 卿又云：「王鐸是敗軍之將，兼征引矍相射義」者。

translations.literal: You also said: "Wang Duo is a general of a defeated army, and moreover cites the archery meaning at Ju Xiang."
translations.idiomatic: You also wrote: "Wang Duo is a defeated general, and you cite the Ju Xiang archery passage against him."

sentences.zh: 昔曹沫三敗，終復魯讎；

translations.literal: Formerly Cao Mo was defeated three times, yet in the end restored Lu's vengeance;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Mo was thrice defeated yet at last avenged Lu;

sentences.zh: 孟明再奔，竟雪秦恥。

translations.literal: Meng Ming fled twice, yet finally cleared Qin's shame.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Ming fled twice yet finally wiped away Qin's shame.

sentences.zh: 近代汾陽尚父，咸寧太師，亦曾不利鼓鼙，尋則功成鐘鼎。

translations.literal: In recent times the Prince-Father of Fenyang and the Grand Preceptor of Xianning also once met with ill fortune at the drums and banners; soon after they achieved merit inscribed on bell and cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: In our own age the Prince-Father of Fenyang and the Grand Preceptor of Xianning also once suffered defeat; soon they won glory recorded in bronze.

sentences.zh: 安知王鐸不立大勛？

translations.literal: How does one know Wang Duo will not establish great achievement?
translations.idiomatic: Who can say Wang Duo will not win great merit?

sentences.zh: 卿又云：「無使百代有抱恨之臣，千古留刮席之恥。

translations.literal: You also said: "Do not let age after age have ministers nursing resentment; for a thousand years leave no disgrace of scraping the mat.
translations.idiomatic: You also wrote: "Do not let future generations inherit embittered ministers and the shame of Liu Bo for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 但慮寇生東土，劉氏復興，即軹道之災，豈獨往日」者。

translations.literal: Only fearing that bandits arise in the eastern lands, the Liu house revives—the disaster of Zhidao, is it confined to days past alone."
translations.idiomatic: I fear only that rebels rise in the east and the Liu house revive—the disaster of Zhidao is not past history alone."

sentences.zh: 我國家景祚方遠，天命未窮，海內人心，尚樂唐德。

translations.literal: Our state's bright fortune is yet far-reaching; Heaven's mandate is not exhausted; hearts within the seas still rejoice in Tang virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's fortune remains bright, the mandate unspent; all within the seas still cherish Tang virtue.

sentences.zh: 朕不荒酒色，不虧刑名，不結怨於生靈，不貪財於宇縣。

translations.literal: I am not dissolute in wine and women, do not fail in punishments and names, do not knot resentment among the living people, do not greedily seek wealth among the domains of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I am not dissolute, I uphold law and justice, I bear no grudge against the people, I do not grasp for wealth across the realm.

sentences.zh: 自知運歷，必保延洪。

translations.literal: I myself know the cycles of fate and surely preserve extended grand flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: I know my destiny and trust the dynasty will endure and flourish.

sentences.zh: 況巡省已來，禎祥薦降；

translations.literal: Moreover, since the tour of inspection, auspicious signs have repeatedly descended;
translations.idiomatic: Since my progress westward, auspicious omens have repeatedly appeared;

sentences.zh: 西蜀半年之內，聲名又以備全。

translations.literal: Within half a year in western Shu, reputation and fame have again been made complete.
translations.idiomatic: Within half a year in western Shu my reputation has been fully restored.

sentences.zh: 塞北、日南，悉來朝貢；

translations.literal: North of the passes and south of the sun, all come to court and tribute;
translations.idiomatic: North and far south alike come to pay tribute;

sentences.zh: 黠戛、善闡，並至梯航。

translations.literal: Qiqar and Shanchan, all arrive by ladder-ships and oared boats.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqar and Shanchan come by land and sea routes alike.

sentences.zh: 但慮天寶、建中，未如今日；

translations.literal: Only worry—the Tianbao and Jianzhong eras were not like today;
translations.idiomatic: Even the Tianbao and Jianzhong troubles were not as grave as today—

sentences.zh: 清宮復國，必有近期。

translations.literal: Clearing the palace and restoring the state will surely have a near term.
translations.idiomatic: Yet recovery of the capital must surely be near.

sentences.zh: 卿雲「劉氏復興」，不知誰為其首？

translations.literal: You say "the Liu house revives"—I do not know who would be its head?
translations.idiomatic: You speak of "a Liu revival"—who do you imagine would lead it?

sentences.zh: 遽言「刮席之恥」，比朕於劉盆子耶？

translations.literal: Hastily speaking of the "disgrace of scraping the mat"—do you compare me to Liu Penzi?
translations.idiomatic: You invoke "the shame of scraping the mat"—do you compare me to Liu Penzi?

sentences.zh: 仍憂「軹道之災」，方朕於秦子嬰也？

translations.literal: Still worrying over the "disaster of Zhidao"—do you liken me to Qin Ziying?
translations.idiomatic: You dread "the disaster of Zhidao"—do you equate me with Qin Ziying?

sentences.zh: 雖稱直行，何太罔誣！

translations.literal: Although it is called straightforward speech, how exceedingly false and slanderous!
translations.idiomatic: For frank speech this is outrageously slanderous!

sentences.zh: 三復斯言，尤深駭異。

translations.literal: Three times reviewing these words, I am especially deeply shocked and astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Reading this again and again, I am deeply appalled.

sentences.zh: 卿又云：「賢才在野，憸人滿朝，致陛下為亡國之君，此子等計將安出？

translations.literal: You also said: "Worthy talent is in the wilds; slanderous men fill the court, causing Your Majesty to become a ruler of a perished state—by what means shall such persons' plans be produced?
translations.idiomatic: You also wrote: "Worthy men remain outside while flatterers fill the court, making Your Majesty a doomed ruler—what remedy do such men propose?

sentences.zh: 伏乞戮賣官鬻爵之輩，征鯁直公正之臣」者。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly begs to execute those who sell offices and peddle ranks, and to summon upright and fair ministers."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that you execute those who sell offices and peddle ranks, and summon upright and fair ministers," you wrote.

sentences.zh: 且唐、虞之世，未必盡是忠良；

translations.literal: Moreover, in the ages of Tang and Yu, not necessarily all were loyal and good;
translations.idiomatic: Even in the age of Yao and Shun not every man was loyal;

sentences.zh: 今巖野之間，安得不遺賢彥？

translations.literal: Now among cliffs and wilds, how could worthy talents not be left behind?
translations.idiomatic: How could worthies not still be overlooked in the hills today?

sentences.zh: 朕每令銓擇，亦遣訪求。

translations.literal: I each time order selection and evaluation, and also send to seek and search.
translations.idiomatic: I constantly order selection and send men to seek talent.

sentences.zh: 其於選將料兵，安人救物，但屬收復之業，講求理化之基，自有長才，同匡大計。

translations.literal: As for choosing generals and calculating troops, settling people and saving things—so long as it belongs to the work of recovery and seeks the foundation of transforming and ordering, there will naturally be long talent to together right the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: For choosing commanders, saving the people, and rebuilding the realm, there will naturally be able men to share the great undertaking.

sentences.zh: 賣官鬻爵之士，中外必不有之，勿聽狂辭，以資遊說。

translations.literal: Men who sell offices and peddle ranks—within and without there certainly are some; do not listen to mad words to provide material for roaming persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: Those who sell offices surely exist here and there—do not heed wild talk meant for agitation.

sentences.zh: 且朕遠違宮闕，寄寓巴邛，所失恩者甚多，尚不興怨，卿落一都統，何足介懷？

translations.literal: Moreover I am far from the palace halls, sojourning at Ba and Qiong; those who have lost favor are many—I still do not raise resentment; you lost one title of overall commander—what is there worth taking to heart?
translations.idiomatic: I am far from the capital, exiled to Ba and Qiong; many have lost favor yet I bear no grudge—why fixate on losing one supreme command?

sentences.zh: 況天步未傾，皇綱尚整，三靈不昧，百度猶存。

translations.literal: Moreover the Heaven's step has not toppled; the imperial net is still orderly; the three spirits are not darkened; the hundred measures still remain.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty has not fallen, order still holds, the spirits have not forsaken us, institutions endure.

sentences.zh: 但守君臣之軌儀，正上下之名分，宜遵教約，未可隳淩。

translations.literal: Only keep the norms of lord and minister, correct the name distinctions of above and below—one should follow teachings and covenants; one must not yet overturn and violate them.
translations.idiomatic: Preserve the rites of lord and minister and the order of rank; keep your sworn duty and do not overstep.

sentences.zh: 朕雖沖人，安得輕侮！

translations.literal: Although I am a young person, how could I be lightly insulted!
translations.idiomatic: Though I am young, I am not to be insulted lightly!

sentences.zh: 但以知卿歲久，許卿分深，貴存終始之恩，忽貯猜嫌之慮。

translations.literal: But because I know your years are long and grant that your intimacy is deep, I value preserving grace from first to last—do not suddenly store up suspicions and resentments.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing our long association and deep bond, I would preserve grace to the end—do not harbor sudden suspicions.

sentences.zh: 所宜深省，無更過言！

translations.literal: What is fitting is deep reflection; do not again have excessive words!
translations.idiomatic: Reflect deeply and speak no more so recklessly!

sentences.zh: 駢始以兵權，欲臨籓鎮，吞並江南；

translations.literal: Pian at first by military power wished to overlook the frontier commands and swallow and merge Jiangnan;
translations.idiomatic: Pian had first used his army to dominate neighboring circuits and swallow the south;

sentences.zh: 一朝失之，威望頓滅，陰謀自阻。

translations.literal: In one morning he lost it; his awe-inspiring power suddenly perished, and his hidden plots by themselves were blocked.
translations.idiomatic: once that authority vanished his prestige collapsed and his schemes failed.

sentences.zh: 故累表堅論，欲其復故。

translations.literal: Therefore he repeatedly memorialized in firm argument, wishing that things return to the former state.
translations.idiomatic: Hence his stubborn memorials demanding restoration of his former powers.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，王鐸與諸道之師敗賊關中，收復京城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the next year Wang Duo and the armies of the circuits defeated the bandits in Guanzhong and recovered the capital city.
translations.idiomatic: The following fourth month Wang Duo and the allied armies defeated the rebels in Guanzhong and retook the capital.

sentences.zh: 駢聞之，悔恨萬狀。

translations.literal: When Pian heard it he regretted and hated in ten thousand forms.
translations.idiomatic: Pian was stricken with remorse.

sentences.zh: 而部下多叛，計無所出，乃托求神仙，屏絕戎政，軍中可否，取決於呂用之。

translations.literal: Yet his subordinates mostly rebelled; he had no plan to issue forth, so he entrusted himself to seeking immortals, screened off military administration, and whether the army permitted or denied—decision fell to Lu Yongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: With many of his officers in revolt and no plan left, he turned to seeking immortality, abandoned military affairs, and let Lu Yongzhi decide everything in camp.

sentences.zh: 光啟初，僖宗再幸山南。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi Emperor Xizong again visited Shannan in felicity.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangqi era Emperor Xizong again fled to Shannan.

sentences.zh: 李襜僭號，偽授駢中書令、諸道兵馬都統、江淮鹽鐵轉運等使。

translations.literal: Li Zhan presumptuously took the era-name and falsely invested Pian as Secretariat Director, overall commander of armies of the circuits, Jiang-Huai salt-and-iron transport commissioner, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: The usurper Li Zhan gave Pian the bogus titles of Director of the Secretariat, overall military commander, and Huai salt-and-transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 駢方怨望，而甘於偽署，稱籓納賄，不絕於途；

translations.literal: Pian was just then resentful and hopeful, yet sweetly accepted the false investiture; he styled himself a vassal and sent bribes, unceasing on the road;
translations.idiomatic: Still bitter at the Tang court, he gladly accepted the rebel appointments and sent tribute along the road without cease;

sentences.zh: 晏安自得，日以神仙為事。

translations.literal: peaceful and secure, self-content, day by day he made immortals his affair.
translations.idiomatic: He rested content in ease and devoted each day to the pursuit of immortality.

sentences.zh: 呂用之又存暨工諸葛殷、張守一有長年之術，駢並署為牙將。

translations.literal: Lu Yongzhi again retained the artisan Zhuge Yin and Zhang Shouyi, who had arts of long years; Pian together appointed them as teeth-generals.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi also introduced the artisans Zhuge Yin and Zhang Shouyi, reputed masters of longevity arts, and Pian made them all staff generals.

sentences.zh: 於府第別建道院，院有迎仙樓、延和閣，高八十尺，飾以珠璣金鈿。

translations.literal: At the government residence he separately built a Daoist abbey; the abbey had a Welcome-Immortals tower and a Extended-Harmony pavilion, eighty feet high, ornamented with pearls, coral, gold, and inlay.
translations.idiomatic: He built a Daoist compound in his mansion with an eighty-foot Welcome Immortals tower and Extended Harmony pavilion adorned in pearls and gold.

sentences.zh: 侍女數百，皆羽衣霓服，和聲度曲，擬之鈞天。

translations.literal: Attendant maidens several hundred, all in feather robes and rainbow garments, harmonized voices and measured tunes, comparing them to the Round Heaven music.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of maids in feathered rainbow robes sang harmonized airs meant to rival the music of heaven.

sentences.zh: 日與用之、殷、守一三人授道家法箓，談論於其間，賓佐罕見其面。

translations.literal: Day by day with Yongzhi, Yin, and Shouyi—the three men—he granted Daoist law registers; they discussed among themselves, and guests and aides rarely saw his face.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he conferred Daoist registers on Yongzhi, Yin, and Shouyi and talked with them behind closed doors; his staff scarcely saw his face.

sentences.zh: 府第有隋煬帝所造門屋數間，俗號中書門，最為宏壯，光啟元年，無故自壞。

translations.literal: The government residence had several gate-houses built by Emperor Yang of Sui; commonly called the Secretariat Gate, they were most grand and strong; in the first year of Guangqi, without cause they collapsed by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: His mansion held several gatehouses built by Emperor Yang of Sui, popularly known as the Secretariat Gate—the grandest on the estate—which inexplicably collapsed in the first year of Guangqi.

sentences.zh: 明年，淮南饑，蝗自西來，行而不飛，浮水緣城而入府第。

translations.literal: The next year Huainan suffered famine; locusts came from the west, marched and did not fly, floated on water along the walls and entered the government residence.
translations.idiomatic: The next year famine struck Huainan; locusts marched in from the west without flying, drifted along the moat, and swarmed into his mansion.

sentences.zh: 道院竹木，一夕如翦，經像幢節，皆嚙去其首。

translations.literal: The Daoist abbey's bamboo and trees, in one night were as if clipped; sutra images and banner-poles—all had their heads gnawed away.
translations.idiomatic: Overnight the compound's bamboo seemed shorn with shears, and the heads of every sutra image and ritual banner were gnawed off.

sentences.zh: 撲之不能止。

translations.literal: Beating them could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Beating them down did no good.

sentences.zh: 旬日之內，蝗自食啖而盡。

translations.literal: Within ten days the locusts themselves ate and devoured one another to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the locusts had devoured one another to the last.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，雨魚。

translations.literal: That year in the ninth month, fish rained.
translations.idiomatic: That September fish fell from the sky.

sentences.zh: 是月十日夜，大星隕於延和閣前，其聲如雷，火光爍地。

translations.literal: On the night of the tenth of that month a great star fell before the Extended-Harmony pavilion; its sound was like thunder, fire-light scintillated over the ground.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the tenth a great star fell before the Extended Harmony pavilion with a thunderous roar and a blaze that lit the ground.

sentences.zh: 自二年十一月雨雪陰晦，至三年二月不解。

translations.literal: From the eleventh month of the second year snow and rain overcast and dim, until the second month of the third year it did not clear.
translations.idiomatic: From the eleventh month of Guangqi year two through the second month of year three unbroken snow and gloom.

sentences.zh: 比歲不稔，食物踴貴，道殣相望，饑骸蔽地。

translations.literal: Year on year the harvest was not ripe; food leapt in price; corpses on the road faced one another; famine skeletons covered the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Harvests failed year after year, prices soared, corpses lined the roads, and the hungry dead covered the fields.

sentences.zh: 是月，浙西周寶為三軍所逐。

translations.literal: That month Zhou Bao of western Zhe was driven out by the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Zhou Bao of western Zhe was ousted by his own army.

sentences.zh: 駢喜，以為妖異當之。

translations.literal: Pian rejoiced, taking it that demonic anomalies were answering for it.
translations.idiomatic: Pian was pleased, believing these portents had claimed another victim.

sentences.zh: 三月，蔡賊過淮口，駢令畢師鐸出軍禦之。

translations.literal: In the third month Cai bandits passed Huai mouth; Pian ordered Bi Shiduo to lead troops out to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Cai rebel Yang Xingmi crossed the Huai ford; Pian sent Bi Shiduo to meet him.

sentences.zh: 師鐸與高郵鎮將張神劍、鄭漢璋等，率行營兵反攻揚州。

translations.literal: Shiduo with Gaoyou garrison commander Zhang Shenjian, Zheng Hanzhang, and the rest, led campaigning troops in reverse attack on Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Instead Shiduo joined the Gaoyou commander Zhang Shenjian and Zheng Hanzhang and turned his campaign army against Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 四月，城陷，師鐸囚駢於道院，召宣州觀察使秦彥為廣陵帥。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the city fell; Shiduo imprisoned Pian in the Daoist abbey and summoned Xuanchou observation commissioner Qin Yan as Guangling commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the city fell; Shiduo held Pian in the Daoist compound and installed Qin Yan of Xuanchou as military governor of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 既而蔡賊楊行密自壽州率兵三萬，乘虛攻城。

translations.literal: Soon after, Cai bandit Yang Xingmi from Shou Prefecture led thirty thousand troops, took advantage of the void and attacked the city.
translations.idiomatic: Then Yang Xingmi marched thirty thousand men from Shouzhou and seized the chance to assault the city.

sentences.zh: 城中米鬥五十千，餓死大半。

translations.literal: In the city a dou of rice was fifty thousand cash; more than half died of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Rice in the city sold for fifty thousand cash a picul, and more than half the population starved.

sentences.zh: 駢家屬並在道院，秦彥供給甚薄，薪蒸亦闕。

translations.literal: Pian's family members were all in the Daoist abbey; Qin Yan's supplies were very thin, firewood and kindling also lacked.
translations.idiomatic: Pian's family remained in the compound while Qin Yan grudged them food and fuel alike.

sentences.zh: 奴仆徹延和閣闌檻煮革帶食之，互相篡啖。

translations.literal: Servants tore down Extended-Harmony pavilion railings and balustrades to boil leather belts to eat; they usurped and devoured one another.
translations.idiomatic: Servants stripped the pavilion balustrades to boil leather belts, and some turned cannibal.

sentences.zh: 駢召從事盧涚謂之曰：「予三朝為國，粗立功名。

translations.literal: Pian summoned staff-member Lu Cui and said to him: "I have served the state through three reigns and roughly established merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Pian summoned his aide Lu Cui and said, "I served three reigns and won some distinction.

sentences.zh: 比擺脫塵埃，自求清凈，非與人世爭利。

translations.literal: Lately shaking off dust and mire, I sought purity for myself, not contending for profit with the human world.
translations.idiomatic: I had only lately sought to shed the world and find peace, not to wrest profit from men.

sentences.zh: 一旦至此，神道其何望耶？」

translations.literal: In a single morning coming to this—what can the divine way look to?"
translations.idiomatic: To come to this in a morning—what hope does Heaven leave me?"

sentences.zh: 掩涕不能已。

translations.literal: He covered his face weeping and could not stop.
translations.idiomatic: He wept without end.

sentences.zh: 初，師鐸之入城也，愛將申及謂駢曰：「逆黨人數不多，即日弛於防禁，願奉令公潛出廣陵，依投支郡，以圖雪恥，賊不足平也。

translations.literal: At first, when Shiduo entered the city, his cherished general Shen Ji said to Pian: "The rebel party's numbers are not many; this very day they slacken in prohibitions and guards—I beg you slip out of Guangling to a neighboring prefecture and plan your revenge; the bandits are not enough to be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiduo first took the city, his trusted officer Shen Ji urged Pian, "The rebels are few and already lax in their guard—I beg you slip out of Guangling to a neighboring prefecture and plan your revenge; they are no match for you.

sentences.zh: 若持疑不決，及旦夕不得在公左右。」

translations.literal: If you hold doubt and do not decide, before long I shall not be able to be at the lord's left and right."
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate I may not remain at your side much longer."

sentences.zh: 駢怯懼，不能行其謀。

translations.literal: Pian was timid and afraid, and could not carry out his scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Pian was too fearful to act.

sentences.zh: 九月，師鐸出城戰敗，慮駢為賊內應，又有尼奉仙，自言通神，謂師鐸曰：「揚府災，當有大人死應之，自此善也。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month Shiduo went out of the city and was defeated in battle; he feared Pian as an inside respondent for the bandits; there was also the nun Fengxian, who declared herself in communion with spirits, and said to Shiduo: "Yang Prefecture's calamity—there ought to be a great man who dies to answer it; from this it will be well."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Shiduo was beaten outside the walls and feared Pian might conspire with the enemy; a nun named Fengxian who claimed communion with spirits told him, "Yangzhou's disaster demands a great man's death; after that all will be well."

sentences.zh: 秦彥曰：「大人非高令公耶？」

translations.literal: Qin Yan said: "The great man—is it not Lord Gao?"
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yan said, "Surely that means Lord Gao?"

sentences.zh: 即令師鐸以兵攻道院。

translations.literal: He at once ordered Shiduo to take troops and attack the Daoist abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered Shiduo to storm the compound.

sentences.zh: 侍者白駢曰：「有賊攻門。」

translations.literal: Attendants informed Pian: "There are bandits attacking the gate."
translations.idiomatic: An attendant told Pian, "Rebels are at the gate."

sentences.zh: 曰：「此秦彥來。」

translations.literal: He said: "This is Qin Yan coming."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "That must be Qin Yan."

sentences.zh: 整衣候之。

translations.literal: He straightened his garments and waited for him.
translations.idiomatic: He dressed to receive him.

sentences.zh: 俄而，亂卒升階，曳駢數之曰：「公上負天子恩，下陷揚州民，淮南塗炭，公之罪也。」

translations.literal: Before long disorderly soldiers mounted the steps, dragged Pian and upbraided him: "My lord, above you betrayed the Son of Heaven's grace; below you plunged Yangzhou's people—Huainan scorched and charred; it is my lord's crime."
translations.idiomatic: Soon mutineers climbed the steps, seized Pian, and denounced him: "Above you betrayed the Son of Heaven; below you ruined Yangzhou—the Huai region burns because of you."

sentences.zh: 駢未暇言，首已墮地矣。

translations.literal: Pian had no time to speak; his head had already fallen to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could answer, his head was on the floor.

sentences.zh: 駢既死，左右奴客逾垣而遁，入行密軍。

translations.literal: After Pian died, attendants and slaves vaulted the wall and fled, entering Xingmi's army.
translations.idiomatic: When Pian was dead his servants scaled the walls and fled to Yang Xingmi's camp.

sentences.zh: 行密聞之，舉軍縞素，繞城大哭者竟日；

translations.literal: When Xingmi heard it he raised for the whole army white hemp, and around the city they wept loudly for a whole day;
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi draped his army in mourning and wept around the walls all day;

sentences.zh: 仍焚紙奠酒，信宿不已。

translations.literal: still burning paper and offering wine, two nights and it did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: burning offerings through two nights without pause.

sentences.zh: 駢與兒侄死於道院，都一坎瘞之，裹之以氈。

translations.literal: Pian and his sons and nephews died in the Daoist abbey; all were buried in one pit and wrapped in felt.
translations.idiomatic: Pian and his kin died in the compound and were heaped in a single pit wrapped in felt.

sentences.zh: 行密入城，以駢孫俞為判官，令主喪事。

translations.literal: Xingmi entered the city, made Pian's grandson Yu a judge, and ordered him to preside over mourning affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi took the city, appointed Pian's grandson Yu as secretary, and charged him with the funeral.

sentences.zh: 葬送未行而俞卒，後故吏鄺師虔收葬之。

translations.literal: Before burial and escort could be carried out Yu died; afterward a former clerk Kuang Shiqian collected and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu died before the burial could take place, and a former officer named Kuang Shiqian later laid them to rest.

sentences.zh: 初，師鐸入城，呂用之、張守一出奔楊行密，詐言所居有金。

translations.literal: At first when Shiduo entered the city, Lu Yongzhi and Zhang Shouyi fled to Yang Xingmi, falsely claiming that where they lived there was gold.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiduo entered the city Yongzhi and Zhang Shouyi fled to Yang Xingmi, claiming their house held gold.

sentences.zh: 行密入城，掘其家地下，得銅人，長三尺余，身被桎梏，釘其心，刻「高駢」二字於胸，蓋以魅道厭勝蠱惑其心，以至族滅。

translations.literal: Xingmi entered the city and dug under their house; he obtained a bronze man more than three feet long, body bound in cangue, nail driven through the heart, engraved "Gao Pian" two characters on the chest—covertly by demon ways, suppression and conquest, sorcery bewitching his heart, reaching even to clan extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi dug beneath their home and found a three-foot bronze figure in fetters with a nail through the heart and "Gao Pian" carved on its chest—the witchcraft by which Yongzhi had bewitched him to ruin.

sentences.zh: 畢師鐸者，曹州冤朐人。

translations.literal: Bi Shiduo was a man of Yuanqu in Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Shiduo was a native of Yuanqu in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 乾符初，與裏人王仙芝嘯聚為盜，相與陷曹、鄆、荊、襄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfu he with fellow-townsmen Wang Xianzhi whistled and gathered as bandits, together seizing Cao, Yun, Jing, and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianfu era he joined his neighbor Wang Xianzhi in outlawry and together they ravaged Cao, Yun, Jing, and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 師鐸善騎射，其徒自為「鷂子」。

translations.literal: Shiduo was skilled at mounted archery; his followers called themselves "Hawk-nestlings."
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo excelled at horsemanship and archery, and his men called themselves "Sparrowhawks."

sentences.zh: 仙芝死，來降高駢。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi died he came and submitted to Gao Pian.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianzhi's death he surrendered to Gao Pian.

sentences.zh: 初敗黃巢於浙西，皆師鐸、梁纘之效也，頗寵待之。

translations.literal: At first defeating Huang Chao in western Zhe—all was the effect of Shiduo and Liang Guan's effort; he greatly favored and treated them.
translations.idiomatic: Pian's early victories over Huang Chao in Zhexi owed chiefly to Shiduo and Liang Guan, and he favored them generously.

sentences.zh: 駢末年惑於呂用之，舊將俞公楚、姚歸禮皆為用之讒構見殺。

translations.literal: In Pian's late years, deluded by Lu Yongzhi, old generals Yu Gongchu and Yao Guili were all by Yongzhi's slander framed and killed.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Pian fell under Yongzhi's sway, and veteran officers Yu Gongchu and Yao Guili were slandered to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 師鐸意不自安，有愛妾復為用之所奪。

translations.literal: Shiduo's mind was not self-at ease; he had a beloved concubine who again was seized by Yongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo grew uneasy, and Yongzhi had already taken his favorite concubine.

sentences.zh: 光啟三年三月，蔡賊楊行密逼淮口，駢令師鐸率三百騎戍高郵。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Guangqi Cai bandit Yang Xingmi pressed Huai mouth; Pian ordered Shiduo to lead three hundred cavalry to garrison Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Guangqi year three Yang Xingmi threatened the Huai ford, and Pian sent Shiduo with three hundred horsemen to hold Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 戍將張神劍亦怒用之，兩人謀自安之計。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Zhang Shenjian also was angry at Yongzhi; the two men plotted a plan for their own security.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander Zhang Shenjian likewise hated Yongzhi, and the two plotted how to save themselves.

sentences.zh: 用之伺知，亟請召還。

translations.literal: Yongzhi observed and knew, and urgently asked that they be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi learned of it and pressed Pian to recall them at once.

sentences.zh: 師鐸母在廣陵，遣信令師鐸遁去。

translations.literal: Shiduo's mother was in Guangling; she sent word ordering Shiduo to flee away.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo's mother, still in Guangling, sent word urging him to flee.

sentences.zh: 或謂師鐸曰：「請殺神劍，並高郵之兵趨府，令公必殺用之為解。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Shiduo: "Pray kill Shenjian, join Gaoyou's troops and hurry to the government residence—the lord will certainly kill Yongzhi as the solution."
translations.idiomatic: One adviser said, "Kill Shenjian, take the Gaoyou troops to the capital, and the Commander will surely kill Yongzhi to settle this."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「不如投徐州，則身存而家保。」

translations.literal: Again he said: "It is not as good as throwing yourself on Xuzhou—then the body is preserved and the family kept safe."
translations.idiomatic: Another said, "Better flee to Xuzhou and save yourself and your kin."

sentences.zh: 師鐸曰：「非計也。

translations.literal: Shiduo said: "These are not plans.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo replied, "Neither plan will do.

sentences.zh: 呂用之誑惑主帥，塗炭生民，七八年來，鬼怨人怒。

translations.literal: Lu Yongzhi beguiled and deluded the commander, scorching and charring the living people; for seven or eight years ghosts resented and men raged.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi has bewitched the Commander and ruined the people for seven or eight years—ghosts and men alike demand his blood.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，安知天不假予誅妖亂而康淮甸耶？」

translations.literal: Today's affair—how do we know Heaven does not lend me the execution of demonic chaos and the peace of the Huai district?"
translations.idiomatic: Who knows whether Heaven has not lent me this day to slay the demon and restore peace to the Huai?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「鄭漢璋是我歸順時副使，常切齒於用之，今率精兵在淮口。

translations.literal: Again he said: "Zheng Hanzhang was my deputy when I submitted; he always gnashed teeth at Yongzhi—now he leads elite troops at Huai mouth.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Zheng Hanzhang was my lieutenant when I surrendered and has long hated Yongzhi; he now commands crack troops at the Huai ford.

sentences.zh: 聞吾此舉，即樂從也。」

translations.literal: Hearing my this move he will at once gladly follow."
translations.idiomatic: He will join me gladly when he hears what I intend."

sentences.zh: 乃趨淮口，與漢璋合，得兵千人。

translations.literal: He then hurried to Huai mouth, united with Hanzhang, and obtained a thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to the Huai ford, joined Hanzhang, and raised a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 又相與至高郵，問計於張神劍。

translations.literal: Again they together went to Gaoyou and asked Shenjian for a plan.
translations.idiomatic: They went together to Gaoyou to consult Zhang Shenjian.

sentences.zh: 神劍曰：「公見事晚耶？

translations.literal: Shenjian said: "My lord, do you see affairs late?
translations.idiomatic: Shenjian said, "Are you only seeing this now, my lord?

sentences.zh: 用之一妖物耳，前受襄王偽命，作鎮廣州，遲留不行，誌圖淮海節鎮。

translations.literal: Yongzhi is a single demonic thing—that before received the Prince of Xiang's false command, acted as military commissioner of Guangzhou, lingered and did not go, and his will plotted Huai-Hai circuit commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi is a mere sorcerer who once took a bogus post from the Prince of Xiang, stalled at Guangzhou, and aimed at ruling the Huai circuit.

sentences.zh: 令公已奪其魄，彼一旦成事，焉能北面事妖物耶！」

translations.literal: The lord has already seized his soul—when he one morning completes the affair, how can he face north and serve a demonic thing!"
translations.idiomatic: You have already broken his spell—once you succeed, how could you bow to such a creature!"

sentences.zh: 即割臂血為盟，推師鐸為盟主，稱大丞相。

translations.literal: He at once cut arm-blood to make alliance, pushed Shiduo as alliance lord, and styled him Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: They drew blood from their arms and swore allegiance, naming Shiduo covenant leader and Grand Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 移檄郡縣，以誅用之、守一、殷為名，乃署其卒長唐宏、王朗、駱玄真、倪詳、逯本、趙簡等，分董其卒三千人。

translations.literal: They shifted proclamations to commanderies and counties, taking as name the execution of Yongzhi, Shouyi, and Yin; then they appointed their squad-chiefs Tang Hong, Wang Lang, Luo Xuanzhen, Ni Xiang, Lu Ben, Zhao Jian, and the rest to divide and oversee their three thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: They issued proclamations across the prefectures in the name of executing Yongzhi, Shouyi, and Yin, and appointed squad leaders Tang Hong, Wang Lang, Luo Xuanzhen, Ni Xiang, Lu Ben, Zhao Jian, and others to command their three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 四月，趨廣陵，營於大明寺，揚州大駭。

translations.literal: In the fourth month they hurried to Guangling, encamped at Daming Temple, and Yangzhou was greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month they marched on Guangling and camped at Daming Temple, throwing Yangzhou into panic.

sentences.zh: 呂用之分兵城守，高駢登延和閣，聞鼓噪聲怪之。

translations.literal: Lu Yongzhi divided troops to guard the city; Gao Pian mounted the Extended-Harmony pavilion and heard drum and clamor sounds and wondered at them.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi deployed the garrison while Pian climbed the Extended Harmony pavilion and wondered at the uproar below.

sentences.zh: 用之曰：「師鐸兵士回戈，止遏不得，適已隨宜處置，公幸勿憂。

translations.literal: Yongzhi said: "Shiduo's soldiers turned their blades back; I could not stop and check them—in passing I have already disposed as fit; my lord, pray do not worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi said, "Shiduo's men have turned their weapons and I could not stop them—I have already handled it as best I could; do not trouble yourself, my lord.

sentences.zh: 茍不聽，徒勞玄女一符耳。」

translations.literal: If you will not heed, it would only waste the Dark Maiden's one talisman."
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse to listen, even the Dark Maiden's talisman will be wasted."

sentences.zh: 師鐸陳兵數日，用之屢出戰，師鐸憂其不克，求救於宣州秦彥曰：「茍得廣陵，則迎公為帥。」

translations.literal: Shiduo arrayed troops for several days; Yongzhi repeatedly went out to battle; Shiduo worried he would not overcome, and begged rescue from Xuanchou's Qin Yan: "If I obtain Guangling, then I will welcome you as commander."
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo besieged the city for days while Yongzhi sallied repeatedly; fearing failure, Shiduo begged Qin Yan of Xuanchou, "If I take Guangling I will install you as governor."

sentences.zh: 彥令牙將秦稠，率兵三千助之。

translations.literal: Yan ordered his teeth-general Qin Chou to lead three thousand troops to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent his officer Qin Chou with three thousand men to help.

sentences.zh: 師鐸門客畢慕顏自城中出，曰：「人心已離，破之必矣！」

translations.literal: Shiduo's gate-guest Bi Muyan came out from the city and said: "Human hearts have already left—breaking it is certain!"
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo's client Bi Muyan slipped out of the city and said, "The people's hearts are gone—you will break it for certain!"

sentences.zh: 秦稠軍至，兵威漸振。

translations.literal: When Qin Chou's army arrived, military prestige gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: When Chou's troops arrived the army's morale rose.

sentences.zh: 駢聞甚憂，謂用之曰：「吾以心腹仗爾，不能駕馭此輩，誤我何多？

translations.literal: Pian heard and was deeply worried; he said to Yongzhi: "I entrusted you as heart-and-belly—yet you cannot rein these fellows; how much have you misled me?
translations.idiomatic: Pian was deeply worried and told Yongzhi, "I trusted you as my own heart—yet you cannot control these men; how you have misled me!

sentences.zh: 百姓遭罹饑饉，不可虐用。

translations.literal: The common people suffer famine and dearth—you must not abuse and use them.
translations.idiomatic: The people are starving—you must not abuse them.

sentences.zh: 吾自枉手劄喻師鐸，可令大將一人自行。」

translations.literal: I myself will wrongly write by hand to instruct Shiduo; you may have one great general go in person."
translations.idiomatic: I will write to Shiduo myself; send a senior officer to deliver it."

sentences.zh: 用之即以其黨許戡送駢書。

translations.literal: Yongzhi at once used his faction-member Xu Kan to deliver Pian's letter.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi sent his henchman Xu Kan with the letter.

sentences.zh: 師鐸怒曰：「梁纘、韓問何在？

translations.literal: Shiduo angrily said: "Where are Liang Guan and Han Wen?
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo raged, "Where are Liang Guan and Han Wen?

sentences.zh: 令爾來耶！」

translations.literal: Did he order you to come!"
translations.idiomatic: Did he send you?"

sentences.zh: 即斬之。

translations.literal: He at once beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He had Kan beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 用之選勁兵自衛。

translations.literal: Yongzhi selected crack troops to guard himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi kept his strongest troops for his own guard.

sentences.zh: 一日至道院，駢叱去之。

translations.literal: One day he came to the Daoist abbey; Pian shouted and drove him away.
translations.idiomatic: One day he entered the compound and Pian drove him out.

sentences.zh: 乃令猶子傑握牙兵，令師鐸母作書，遣大將古鍔與師鐸子出城喻之。

translations.literal: He then ordered his nephew's son Jie to grasp the teeth-army; he had Shiduo's mother compose a letter and sent the great general Gu E and Shiduo's son out of the city to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: He put his nephew Jie in command of the guard, had Shiduo's mother write a letter, and sent the general Gu E with Shiduo's son to reason with him outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 師鐸令子還，白曰：「不敢負令公恩德，正為淮南除弊。

translations.literal: Shiduo ordered his son to return and report: "I dare not betray the lord's grace and virtue—I am just now ridding Huainan of abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo sent his son back with the message, "I do not forget the Commander's kindness—I act only to purge Huainan's evils.

sentences.zh: 但斬用之、守一，即日退還高郵。」

translations.literal: But if you behead Yongzhi and Shouyi, this very day I will withdraw and return to Gaoyou."
translations.idiomatic: Kill Yongzhi and Shouyi and I will withdraw to Gaoyou the same day."

sentences.zh: 秦稠攻西南隅，城中應之，即日城陷。

translations.literal: Qin Chou attacked the southwest corner; inside the city they answered him—the same day the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Chou struck the southwest wall, insiders opened the gates, and the city fell that day.

sentences.zh: 呂用之由參佐門遁走。

translations.literal: Lu Yongzhi fled through the aide's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi fled through the aides' gate.

sentences.zh: 駢聞師鐸至，改服俟之，與師鐸交拜，如賓主之儀。

translations.literal: Pian heard Shiduo had come, changed garments and waited for him, and with Shiduo exchanged bows like host and guest rites.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Shiduo had come, Pian dressed to receive him and they bowed to each other as host and guest.

sentences.zh: 即日署為節度副使，漢璋、神劍皆署職事。

translations.literal: That same day he appointed him as deputy military commissioner; Hanzhang and Shenjian were all given official posts.
translations.idiomatic: That day he named Shiduo deputy military governor and gave Hanzhang and Shenjian offices.

sentences.zh: 秦稠點閱府庫，監守之，仍密召彥於宣州。

translations.literal: Qin Chou inspected and reviewed the government treasury, kept guard over it, and still secretly summoned Yan from Xuanchou.
translations.idiomatic: Chou inventoried the treasury under guard and secretly summoned Yan from Xuanchou.

sentences.zh: 或謂師鐸曰：「公昨舉兵誅二妖物，故人情樂從。

translations.literal: Someone said to Shiduo: "Yesterday you raised troops to execute the two demonic things—therefore men's hearts gladly followed.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Shiduo, "You raised the army to kill the sorcerers and the people followed gladly.

sentences.zh: 今軍府已安，以事理論之，公宜還政高公，自典兵馬，戎權在手，取舍自由，籓鄰聞之，不失大義。

translations.literal: Now the army government is already secure; weighing things by principle, you ought to return government to Lord Gao, yourself direct troops and horses—with military authority in hand, choosing and discarding freely—neighboring circuits hearing it would not lose great righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Now the government is secure; by rights you should restore power to Lord Gao and keep command of the troops yourself—neighboring circuits would call that honorable.

sentences.zh: 議者皆言秦稠破城之日，已召秦彥。

translations.literal: Those in discussion all said that on the day Qin Chou broke the city he had already summoned Qin Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Many said Chou had already summoned Yan on the day the city fell.

sentences.zh: 彥若為帥，兵權非足下有也。

translations.literal: If Yan becomes commander, military authority will not be under your feet.
translations.idiomatic: If Yan becomes governor you will hold no military power.

sentences.zh: 公感其援，但以金玉報之，阻其渡江，最為上策。

translations.literal: My lord, moved by his aid, need only repay with gold and jade, block his crossing the river—that is the highest strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Repay his aid with gold and jade and keep him from crossing the river—that is the best course.

sentences.zh: 若秦彥作帥，則楊行密朝聞夕至。

translations.literal: If Qin Yan becomes commander, then Yang Xingmi, hearing in the morning, will arrive by evening.
translations.idiomatic: If Yan takes command Yang Xingmi will be upon you by nightfall.

sentences.zh: 如高令復帥，外寇必自卷懷。」

translations.literal: If Lord Gao again becomes commander, outer bandits will surely of themselves roll up their bosoms."
translations.idiomatic: If Lord Gao rules again the outside enemy will withdraw on his own."

sentences.zh: 師鐸猶豫未決，而秦彥軍至。

translations.literal: Shiduo hesitated and had not decided, yet Qin Yan's army arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo still wavered when Yan's army arrived.

sentences.zh: 五月，彥為節度使，署師鐸為行軍司馬，移居牙外，心頗不悅。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Yan became military commissioner; he appointed Shiduo campaigning marshal and moved him to quarters outside the headquarters compound; at heart he was quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Qin Yan took the post of military commissioner. He named Bi Shiduo campaigning marshal but quartered him outside the yamen—a slight Shiduo deeply resented.

sentences.zh: 是月，楊行密引軍攻揚州，彥兵拒戰繼敗。

translations.literal: That month, Yang Xingmi led troops to attack Yangzhou; Yan's soldiers resisted in battle and were defeated in succession.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Yang Xingmi marched on Yangzhou. Qin Yan's forces fought him off repeatedly and lost every engagement.

sentences.zh: 八月，師鐸與鄭漢璋出軍萬人擊行密，皆大敗而還，自是不復出。
