translations.literal: In the eighth month, Shiduo together with Zheng Hanzhang sent out an army of ten thousand men to strike Xingmi; all were utterly defeated and returned; from then on they did not go out again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Bi Shiduo and Zheng Hanzhang led ten thousand men against Yang Xingmi and were routed. After that they never sallied from the city again.

sentences.zh: 九月，師鐸殺高駢。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Shiduo killed Gao Pian.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Bi Shiduo killed Gao Pian.

sentences.zh: 十月，秦彥、師鐸突圍而遁。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Qin Yan and Shiduo broke through the encirclement and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Qin Yan and Bi Shiduo burst through the siege lines and escaped.

sentences.zh: 十一月，秦彥、師鐸引蔡賊孫儒之兵三萬圍揚州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Qin Yan and Shiduo brought the Cai bandit Sun Ru's army of thirty thousand to besiege Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they summoned Sun Ru—thirty thousand men from the Cai rebels—to join them in besieging Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 行密求救於汴，硃全忠遣大將李璠率師淮口，以為聲援。

translations.literal: Xingmi sought rescue from Bian; Zhu Quanzhong sent the great general Li Fan to lead troops at the Huai Estuary as a demonstration of support.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi appealed to Bianliang. Zhu Quanzhong dispatched his general Li Fan with an army to the Huai Estuary as a show of force.

sentences.zh: 孫儒以廣陵未下，而汴卒來，又慮秦彥、師鐸異志。

translations.literal: Sun Ru, because Guangling had not been taken and Bian troops had come, also feared that Qin Yan and Shiduo harbored divergent intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru still could not take Guangling, saw Bian troops arriving, and began to fear that Qin Yan and Bi Shiduo might turn against him.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，孫儒斬秦彥、師鐸於高郵之南，鄭漢璋亦死焉。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, Sun Ru beheaded Qin Yan and Shiduo south of Gaoyou; Zheng Hanzhang also died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year Sun Ru executed Qin Yan and Bi Shiduo south of Gaoyou. Zheng Hanzhang perished in the same purge.

sentences.zh: 附 秦彥秦彥者，徐州人，本名立。

translations.literal: Supplement: Qin Yan. Qin Yan was a man of Xuzhou; his original name was Li.
translations.idiomatic: [Supplement:] Qin Yan was a native of Xuzhou; his birth name was Li.

sentences.zh: 為卒，隸徐軍。

translations.literal: He became a soldier and was attached to the Xu army.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted as a common soldier in the Xu garrison.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，坐盜繫獄，將死，夢人謂之曰：「爾可隨我。」

translations.literal: In the Qianfu era, for theft he was imprisoned; about to die, in a dream a person said to him: "You may follow me."
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianfu reign he was jailed for theft and condemned to die. In a dream a voice told him, "Come with me."

sentences.zh: 及寤，械破，乃得逸去，因改名彥。

translations.literal: When he awoke, his fetters were broken; he thus escaped, and therefore changed his name to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke, his shackles had split apart. He fled, and from then on called himself Yan.

sentences.zh: 乃聚徒百人，殺下邳令，取其資裝入黃巢軍。

translations.literal: He then gathered a band of a hundred men, killed the magistrate of Xiapi, took his goods and equipment, and entered Huang Chao's army.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied a hundred followers, slew the magistrate of Xiapi, seized his supplies, and joined Huang Chao's horde.

sentences.zh: 巢兵敗於淮南，乃與許勍俱降高駢，累奏授和州刺史。

translations.literal: When Chao's army was defeated in Huainan, he together with Xu Zhou both surrendered to Gao Pian; through repeated memorials he was appointed prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebel defeat in Huainan he surrendered to Gao Pian with Xu Zhou and was eventually memorialized into office as prefect of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 中和二年，宣歙觀察使竇潏病，彥以兵襲取之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe, the Xuanshe observation commissioner Dou Yu fell ill; Yan seized it with troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhonghe, when Dou Yu, observation commissioner of Xuanshe, fell ill, Yan seized the command by force.

sentences.zh: 遂代潏為觀察使，朝廷因而命之。

translations.literal: He then replaced Yu as observation commissioner; the court thereupon confirmed the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He supplanted Dou Yu as observation commissioner, and the court ratified his seizure.

sentences.zh: 光啟三年，揚州牙將畢師鐸囚其帥高駢，懼外寇來侵，乃迎彥為帥。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangqi, the Yangzhou garrison officer Bi Shiduo imprisoned his commander Gao Pian; fearing invasion by outside foes, he therefore welcomed Yan as commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangqi, Bi Shiduo, a Yangzhou garrison officer, imprisoned his commander Gao Pian. Fearing outside attack, he invited Qin Yan to take command.

sentences.zh: 彥召池州刺史趙锽知宣州事，自率眾入揚州。

translations.literal: Yan summoned the Chizhou prefect Zhao Hui to administer Xuancheng affairs and personally led his host into Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan appointed Zhao Hui, prefect of Chizhou, to govern Xuanzhou and marched his main force into Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 師鐸推彥為帥。

translations.literal: Shiduo promoted Yan as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Shiduo had Yan proclaimed commander.

sentences.zh: 五月，壽州刺史楊行密率兵攻彥，遣其將張神劍令統兵屯灣頭山光寺。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Shouzhou prefect Yang Xingmi led troops to attack Yan; he sent his general Zhang Shenjian to command troops stationed at the Guang Temple on Wanto Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yang Xingmi, prefect of Shouzhou, attacked Qin Yan. He posted his general Zhang Shenjian at the Guang Temple on Mount Wanto.

sentences.zh: 行密屯大雲寺，北跨長崗，前臨大道，自楊子江北至槐家橋，柵壘相聯。

translations.literal: Xingmi encamped at the Dayun Temple, spanning the long ridge to the north, facing the great road in front; from north of the Yangzi River embankment to Huaijia Bridge, palisades and ramparts were linked in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi made his camp at the Dayun Temple, anchoring his line along the long ridge north of the city and facing the main road. From the north bank of the Yangzi to Huaijia Bridge his fortifications ran unbroken.

sentences.zh: 秦彥登城望之，懼形於色。

translations.literal: Qin Yan ascended the wall to look upon them; fear showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yan climbed the wall to look out and could not hide his terror.

sentences.zh: 令秦稠、師鐸率勁卒八千出鬥，為行密所掩，盡沒。

translations.literal: He ordered Qin Chou and Shiduo to lead eight thousand crack troops out to fight; they were ambushed by Xingmi and all were lost.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qin Chou and Bi Shiduo out with eight thousand elite troops; Yang Xingmi ambushed them and wiped out the sortie.

sentences.zh: 稠死之。

translations.literal: Chou died in the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Chou fell in the fight.

sentences.zh: 彥急求援於蘇州刺史張雄。

translations.literal: Yan urgently sought aid from the Suzhou prefect Zhang Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yan desperately appealed to Zhang Xiong, prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 雄率兵赴之，屯於東塘。

translations.literal: Xiong led troops to go to his aid and encamped at Dongtang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiong marched to his relief and encamped at Dongtang.

sentences.zh: 重圍半年，城中芻糧並盡，草根木實、市肆藥物、皮囊革帶，食之亦盡。

translations.literal: Under heavy siege for half a year, within the city fodder and grain were utterly exhausted; roots of grass, fruits of trees, drugs from market stalls, and leather bags and belts were eaten until gone as well.
translations.idiomatic: After six months under siege the city had no fodder or grain left. People ate grass roots, tree fruit, apothecary stock, even leather pouches and belts until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 外軍掠人而賣，人五十千。

translations.literal: The outside army seized people and sold them; a person cost fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The besiegers kidnapped civilians and sold them—fifty thousand cash for a life.

sentences.zh: 死者十六七，縱存者鬼形鳥面，氣息奄然。

translations.literal: Of the dead, six or seven in ten; even those who survived had ghostly forms and bird-like faces, their breath barely lingering.
translations.idiomatic: Six or seven in ten were dead. Survivors were wasted to ghostly frames and hawk faces, barely breathing.

sentences.zh: 張雄多軍糧，相約交市。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiong had much military grain; they agreed to trade with each other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiong held ample military grain, and the two sides arranged to trade.

sentences.zh: 城中以寶貝市米，金一斤，通犀帶一，得米五升。

translations.literal: Within the city they used valuables to buy rice: one jin of gold, one rhinoceros-horn belt—for these they obtained five sheng of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the walls treasure bought rice: one pound of gold or a rhinoceros-horn belt fetched five pints.

sentences.zh: 雄軍得貨，不戰而去。

translations.literal: Xiong's army obtained goods and departed without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiong's men took their payment and marched away without a battle.

sentences.zh: 九月，畢師鐸出戰，又敗。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Bi Shiduo went out to battle and was defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Bi Shiduo sallied forth and lost again.

sentences.zh: 自是日與秦彥相對嗟惋。

translations.literal: From then on, day by day he and Qin Yan faced each other sighing in lament.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he and Qin Yan spent their days together in mutual lament.

sentences.zh: 問神尼奉仙何以獲濟，尼曰：「走為上計也。」

translations.literal: They asked the divine nun Fengxian how they might obtain deliverance; the nun said: "Flight is the superior plan."
translations.idiomatic: They asked the nun Fengxian how they might be saved. She said, "Running away is your best chance."

sentences.zh: 十月，彥與師鐸突圍投孫儒，並為所殺。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Yan and Shiduo broke through the siege and threw themselves upon Sun Ru; both were killed by him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Qin Yan and Bi Shiduo broke out and fled to Sun Ru—and he killed them both.

sentences.zh: 江淮之間，廣陵大鎮，富甲天下。

translations.literal: Between the Jiang and Huai, Guangling was a great stronghold, its wealth foremost in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Yangtze and the Huai, Guangling was a great metropolis, wealthiest in the empire.

sentences.zh: 自師鐸、秦彥之後，孫儒、行密繼踵相攻，四五年間，連兵不息，廬舍焚蕩，民戶喪亡，廣陵之雄富掃地矣！

translations.literal: After Shiduo and Qin Yan, Sun Ru and Xingmi followed in succession attacking one another; within four or five years, armies fought without cease; dwellings were burned and swept away, households perished; Guangling's heroic wealth was swept clean to the ground!
translations.idiomatic: After Bi Shiduo and Qin Yan came Sun Ru and Yang Xingmi, each in turn laying siege to the city. For four or five years war never stopped. Houses burned, families vanished, and Guangling's grandeur was utterly erased.

sentences.zh: 時溥

translations.literal: =Shi Pu=
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu

sentences.zh: 時溥，彭城人，徐之牙將。

translations.literal: Shi Pu was a man of Pengcheng, a garrison officer of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu was a native of Pengcheng and a garrison officer of the Xu command.

sentences.zh: 黃巢據長安，詔征天下兵進討。

translations.literal: Huang Chao held Chang'an; an edict summoned armies from across the realm to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao held Chang'an, the throne ordered armies from across the empire to march against him.

sentences.zh: 中和二年，武寧軍節度使支詳遣溥與副將陳璠率師五千赴難。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe, the Wuning military commissioner Zhi Xiang sent Pu together with deputy general Chen Fan to lead five thousand troops to the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhonghe, Zhi Xiang, military commissioner of Wuning, sent Shi Pu and his deputy Chen Fan with five thousand men to answer the imperial call.

sentences.zh: 行至河陰，軍亂，剽河陰縣回。

translations.literal: When they reached Heyin, the army mutinied, plundered Heyin County, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyin the column mutinied, looted the county, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 溥招合撫諭，其眾復集，懼罪，屯於境上。

translations.literal: Pu gathered them and comforted them with persuasion; his host reassembled; fearing punishment, they encamped on the border.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu rallied and reassured them until the force re-formed. Still fearing court punishment, they halted on the border of Xu territory.

sentences.zh: 詳遣人迎犒，悉恕之，溥乃移軍向徐州。

translations.literal: Xiang sent men to welcome and reward them; he wholly pardoned them; Pu then moved his army toward Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Xiang sent envoys with gifts and pardon. Shi Pu then marched on Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 既入，軍人大呼，推溥為留後，送詳於大彭館。

translations.literal: Once inside, the soldiers shouted loudly, promoted Pu as acting commander, and sent Xiang to the Dapeng Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside the city the troops acclaimed him acting commander and lodged Zhi Xiang at the Dapeng guesthouse.

sentences.zh: 溥大出資裝，遣陳璠援詳歸京。

translations.literal: Pu gave out great quantities of goods and equipment, dispatched Chen Fan to escort Xiang back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu lavished gifts upon him and sent Chen Fan to escort Zhi Xiang back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 詳宿七里亭，其夜為璠所殺，舉家屠害。

translations.literal: Xiang lodged at Qili Pavilion; that night he was killed by Fan; his entire family was slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Xiang stopped at Qili Pavilion. That night Chen Fan murdered him and slaughtered his entire family.

sentences.zh: 溥以璠為宿州刺史，竟以違命殺詳。

translations.literal: Pu appointed Fan prefect of Suzhou; in the end, for disobeying orders, Fan killed Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu named Chen Fan prefect of Su Prefecture—even though Fan had murdered Zhi Xiang in open defiance of his commander.

sentences.zh: 溥誅璠，又令別將帥軍三千赴難京師。

translations.literal: Pu executed Fan, and again ordered another general to lead three thousand troops to the capital in its crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu then executed Chen Fan and sent another officer with three thousand men to aid the capital.

sentences.zh: 天子還宮，授之節鉞。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven returned to the palace; [the court] granted him the command seal and staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the palace, the court invested him with the command seal and staff.

sentences.zh: 及黃巢攻陳州，秦宗權據蔡州，與賊連結。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao attacked Chenzhou, Qin Zongquan held Caizhou and linked with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao besieged Chenzhou, Qin Zongquan held Caizhou and allied with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 徐、蔡相近，溥出師討之。

translations.literal: Xu and Cai were adjacent; Pu led troops out to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Cai lay side by side, so Shi Pu marched out against him.

sentences.zh: 軍鋒益盛，每戰屢捷。

translations.literal: The army's edge grew ever keener; in every battle repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: His army grew ever stronger and won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 黃巢之敗也，其將尚讓以數千人降溥，後林言又斬黃巢首歸徐州，時溥功居第一，詔授檢校太尉、中書令、鉅鹿郡王。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao was defeated, his general Shang Rang surrendered to Pu with several thousand men; later Lin Yan again beheaded Huang Chao and brought his head back to Xuzhou; at that time Pu's merit ranked first; an edict appointed him acting Grand Preceptor, Grand Councilor, and Prince of Julu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Chao's fall his general Shang Rang surrendered to Shi Pu with several thousand men. Later Lin Yan sent Huang Chao's head to Xuzhou. The court ranked Shi Pu's merit first and made him acting Grand Preceptor, Grand Councilor, and Prince of Julu.

sentences.zh: 宗權未平，仍授溥徐州行營兵馬都統。

translations.literal: Zongquan not yet pacified, [the court] still appointed Pu as overall commander of Xuzhou field-camp horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: With Zongquan still undefeated, the court also named him overall commander of the Xu field armies.

sentences.zh: 蔡賊平，朱全忠與之爭功，遂相嫌怨。

translations.literal: The Cai bandits pacified, Zhu Quanzhong disputed merit with him; they thus bore mutual resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Cai rebels were crushed, Zhu Quanzhong quarreled with him over credit, and the two came to hate each other.

sentences.zh: 淮南亂，朝廷以全忠遙領淮南節度，以平孫儒、行密之亂。

translations.literal: Huainan was in turmoil; the court had Quanzhong remotely hold the Huainan military commission to pacify the disorders of Sun Ru and Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan fell into chaos the court gave Zhu Quanzhong the Huainan commission in absentia to suppress Sun Ru and Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 汴人應援，路出徐方，溥阻之。

translations.literal: Bian men came to aid; their route passed through Xu territory; Pu blocked them.
translations.idiomatic: Bian troops marched to help, but their route crossed Xu lands—and Shi Pu barred the way.

sentences.zh: 全忠怒，出師攻徐。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was angry and led troops out to attack Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong flew into a rage and marched on Xu.

sentences.zh: 自光啟至大順六七年間，汴軍四集，徐、泗三郡，民無耕稼，頻歲水災，人喪十六七。

translations.literal: From Guangqi to Dazhun, within six or seven years, Bian armies gathered four times; in the three prefectures of Xu and Si the people had no plowing or harvest; year after year flood disasters; people lost six or seven in ten.
translations.idiomatic: For six or seven years from Guangqi through Dazhun the Bian armies invaded again and again. Across Xu and the two Si prefectures farming ceased, floods came year after year, and six or seven in ten of the people perished.

sentences.zh: 溥窘蹙，求和於汴。

translations.literal: Pu was cornered and pressed; he sought peace from Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Shi Pu sued for peace with Bian.

sentences.zh: 全忠曰：「移鎮則可。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong said: "If you transfer your commission, it can be done."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong said, "You may have peace if you surrender your command."

sentences.zh: 然之。

translations.literal: He assented.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu agreed.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以尚書劉崇望代溥，以溥為太子太師。

translations.literal: The court used the Minister Liu Chongwang to replace Pu; Pu was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Minister Liu Chongwang to replace him and named Shi Pu Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 溥懼出城見害，不受代。

translations.literal: Pu feared that leaving the city he would meet harm; he did not accept replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing murder if he left the city, Shi Pu refused to step down.

sentences.zh: 汴將龐師古陳兵於野，溥求援於兗州。

translations.literal: The Bian general Pang Shigu arrayed troops in the open country; Pu sought aid from Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian general Pang Shigu drew up his army in the field while Shi Pu appealed to Yanzhou for help.

sentences.zh: 朱瑾出兵救之，值大雪，糧盡而還。

translations.literal: Zhu Jin led troops out to rescue him; they encountered heavy snow; grain was exhausted and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin marched to his relief, but blizzards exhausted their supplies and forced them back.

sentences.zh: 城中守陴者饑甚，加之病疫。

translations.literal: Within the city those defending the walls were extremely hungry; moreover there was epidemic disease.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders on the walls were starving, and plague swept the city.

sentences.zh: 汴將王重師、牛存節夜乘梯而入，溥與妻子登樓自焚而卒，景福二年四月也。

translations.literal: The Bian generals Wang Chongshi and Niu Cunjie at night climbed ladders and entered; Pu with wife and children ascended a tower, self-immolated, and died—it was the fourth month of the second year of Jingfu.
translations.idiomatic: By night the Bian generals Wang Chongshi and Niu Cunjie scaled the walls on ladders. Shi Pu climbed a tower with his wife and children and burned himself to death in the fourth month of the second year of Jingfu.

sentences.zh: 地入於汴。

translations.literal: The territory passed into Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Xu passed into Bian hands.

sentences.zh: 朱瑄

translations.literal: =Zhu Xuan=
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan

sentences.zh: 朱瑄，宋州人。

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan was a man of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan was a native of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 父慶，盜鹽抵法。

translations.literal: His father Qing stole salt and ran afoul of the law.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qing was convicted for salt smuggling.

sentences.zh: 瑄逃於青州，為王敬武牙卒。

translations.literal: Xuan fled to Qingzhou and became Wang Jingwu's garrison soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan fled to Qingzhou and enlisted as a garrison soldier under Wang Jingwu.

sentences.zh: 中和初，黃巢據長安，詔征天下兵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe, Huang Chao held Chang'an; an edict summoned armies from across the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhonghe reign Huang Chao held Chang'an and the throne called up armies from across the empire.

sentences.zh: 敬武遣牙將曹全晸率兵三千赴難關西，以瑄為軍候。

translations.literal: Jingwu sent the garrison officer Cao Quanzhen to lead three thousand troops west to the crisis in the passes, making Xuan army adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwu sent his officer Cao Quanzhen west with three thousand men and made Xuan his army adjutant.

sentences.zh: 會青州警急，敬武召全晸還，路由鄆州。

translations.literal: When Qingzhou's alarm was urgent, Jingwu recalled Quanzhen; their route passed through Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingzhou itself came under threat Jingwu recalled Quanzhen, and the column marched back through Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時鄆帥薛崇為草賊王仙芝所殺，鄆將崔君裕權知州事。

translations.literal: At that time the Yan commander Xue Chong was killed by the grass-bandit Wang Xianzhi; the Yan officer Cui Junyu provisionally administered prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan commander Xue Chong had been killed by the rebel Wang Xianzhi, and the Yan officer Cui Junyu was acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 全晸知其兵寡，襲殺君裕，據有鄆州，自稱留後。

translations.literal: Quanzhen knew their troops were few; he surprised and killed Junyu, seized Yanzhou, and styled himself acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how few defenders Yan had, Quanzhen ambushed and killed Cui Junyu, seized Yanzhou, and proclaimed himself acting commander.

sentences.zh: 以瑄有功，署為濮州刺史，留將牙軍。

translations.literal: Because Xuan had merit, [Quanzhen] appointed him prefect of Puzhou and left him to command the garrison army.
translations.idiomatic: For his service Quanzhen made Xuan prefect of Pu and left him in command of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 光啟初，魏博韓簡欲兼並曹鄆，以兵濟河收鄆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi, Weibo's Han Jian wished to annex Cao and Yan; with troops he crossed the river to take Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangqi Han Jian of Weibo tried to swallow Cao and Yan and crossed the Yellow River to seize Yan.

sentences.zh: 全晸出兵逆戰，為魏軍所敗，全晸死之。

translations.literal: Quanzhen led troops out to oppose battle; he was defeated by the Wei army; Quanzhen died in it.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhen marched out to meet him, was routed by the Wei army, and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 瑄收合殘卒，保州城。

translations.literal: Xuan gathered remnant soldiers and held the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan rallied the survivors and held the walled city.

sentences.zh: 韓簡攻圍半年，不能拔。

translations.literal: Han Jian besieged for half a year and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian besieged it for half a year without success.

sentences.zh: 會魏軍亂，退去。

translations.literal: When the Wei army mutinied, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei troops mutinied they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，授以節鉞。

translations.literal: The court praised this and granted him the command seal and staff.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended his defense and invested him with the command seal and staff.

sentences.zh: 時瑄有眾三萬。

translations.literal: At that time Xuan had a host of thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xuan commanded thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 其弟瑾，勇冠三軍，有爭天下之心。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jin, courage foremost in the three armies, had a mind to contend for All Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhu Jin was the bravest man in the army and dreamed of seizing the realm.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權之盛也，屢侵鄭、汴。

translations.literal: When Qin Zongquan was ascendant, he repeatedly invaded Zheng and Bian.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of Qin Zongquan's power he raided Zheng and Bian again and again.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠為賊所攻，甚窘，求救於瑄。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong was attacked by bandits and was very cornered; he sought rescue from Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong, hard pressed by the rebels, begged Xuan for help.

sentences.zh: 瑄令硃瑾出師援之。

translations.literal: Xuan ordered Zhu Jin to lead troops out to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent Zhu Jin to his relief.

sentences.zh: 擊敗秦宗權，全忠乃與瑄情極隆厚。

translations.literal: They defeated Qin Zongquan; Quanzhong then with Xuan had feelings extremely deep and thick.
translations.idiomatic: Jin routed Qin Zongquan, and Zhu Quanzhong grew closer to Xuan than ever.

sentences.zh: 全忠狡譎翻覆，虎視籓鄰。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was cunning and treacherous, turning his coat; he tiger-eyed neighboring fan domains.
translations.idiomatic: But Quanzhong was treacherous and fickle, eyeing neighboring circuits like prey.

sentences.zh: 會宗權誅，乃急攻徐州。

translations.literal: When Zongquan was executed, [Quanzhong] then urgently attacked Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zongquan was dead he turned at once to besiege Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時溥求援於瑄，瑄與全忠書，請釋溥修好，偽許之。

translations.literal: Shi Pu sought aid from Xuan; Xuan wrote Quanzhong, asking to release Pu and restore good relations; [Quanzhong] falsely promised.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu appealed to Xuan, who wrote Zhu Quanzhong urging him to spare Pu and make peace. Quanzhong pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 瑄以恩及全忠，遣使讓之，又令硃瑾出軍援溥。

translations.literal: Xuan, because of grace owed to Quanzhong, sent an envoy to reprove him; again he ordered Zhu Jin to lead troops out to aid Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Reminding Quanzhong of past favors, Xuan sent envoys to rebuke him and again dispatched Zhu Jin to aid Shi Pu.

sentences.zh: 及徐、泗平，全忠乃移兵攻鄆。

translations.literal: When Xu and Si were pacified, Quanzhong then shifted troops to attack Yan.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu and Si fell he turned his armies on Yan.

sentences.zh: 三四年間，每春秋入其境剽掠，人不得耕織，民為俘者十五六，瑄禦備殫竭。

translations.literal: Within three or four years, each spring and autumn [troops] entered their territory to plunder; people could not farm or weave; people taken captive, six or seven in ten; Xuan's defenses were utterly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: For three or four years his men raided Yan every spring and autumn. Farming and weaving ceased, six or seven in ten of the people were carried off as captives, and Xuan's defenses were worn to nothing.

sentences.zh: 景福末，與弟瑾合兩鎮之兵，與汴人大戰於魚山下，瑄、瑾俱敗，兵士陷沒。

translations.literal: At the end of Jingfu, together with his younger brother Jin he combined the armies of two circuits and fought a great battle with the Bian troops below Mount Yu; Xuan and Jin were both defeated and the soldiers were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jingfu he and his brother Jin united two circuits' forces and met the Bian army at Mount Yu; both brothers were crushed and their troops destroyed.

sentences.zh: 汴將朱友裕以長塹圍之。

translations.literal: The Bian general Zhu Youyu hemmed them in with a long trench.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youyu of Bian penned them in behind a long trench.

sentences.zh: 乾寧四年正月，城中食竭，瑄與妻榮氏出奔，至中都，為野人所害，傳首汴州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Qianning food in the city was exhausted; Xuan fled with his wife Lady Rong; reaching Zhongdu he was killed by country folk, and his head was sent to Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Qianning year four, with the city starving, Xuan fled with Lady Rong; at Zhongdu villagers killed him and sent his head to Bian.

sentences.zh: 榮氏至汴州為尼。

translations.literal: Lady Rong came to Bian Prefecture and became a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Rong reached Bian and took the veil.

sentences.zh: 瑄母弟 瑾朱瑾，瑄之母弟，驍果善戰。

translations.literal: Xuan's younger brother by the same mother, Jin—Zhu Jin, Xuan's uterine younger brother, was fierce and bold and skilled in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin, Xuan's younger brother by the same mother, was a daring and formidable fighter.

sentences.zh: 初，乾符末，朝廷以將軍齊克讓為兗州節度。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Qianfu, the court made the general Qi Kerang military commissioner of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qianfu the court appointed General Qi Kerang military commissioner of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 瑾將襲取之，乃求婚於克讓。

translations.literal: Jin was about to seize it by surprise and therefore sought marriage with Kerang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin planned a surprise takeover and asked for Kerang's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 及親迎，瑾選勇士衛從，禮會之夜竊發，逐克讓，遂據城稱留後。

translations.literal: When he came to welcome the bride, Jin chose brave warriors as escort; on the night of the wedding feast he struck secretly, drove out Kerang, and thereupon held the city and declared himself acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the wedding he brought picked warriors; that night he rose in secret, expelled Kerang, seized the city, and proclaimed himself acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不獲已，以節鉞授之。

translations.literal: The court, having no choice, granted him the seal and baton.
translations.idiomatic: The court could do nothing but confirm his commission.

sentences.zh: 及朱瑄平，汴人移兵攻兗，經年食盡，瑾出城求食。

translations.literal: When Zhu Xuan was pacified, the Bian troops shifted their army to attack Yan; after a year food was exhausted and Jin went out of the city to seek provisions.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuan fell, Bian turned on Yanzhou; a year later supplies ran out and Jin left the city to forage.

sentences.zh: 比還，為別將所拒，不得入。

translations.literal: By the time he returned, another commander barred him and he could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, another officer refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 乃渡淮依楊行密。

translations.literal: Thereupon he crossed the Huai and placed himself under Yang Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Huai and joined Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 行密寵待之，用為壽州刺史，大敗汴軍於清口，自此全忠不敢以兵渡淮。

translations.literal: Xingmi favored and treated him well, employed him as prefect of Shou, and inflicted a great defeat on the Bian army at Qingkou; from this time Quanzhong did not dare send troops across the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi favored him, made him prefect of Shou, and at Qingkou crushed the Bian army so thoroughly that Quanzhong never again dared cross the Huai in force.

sentences.zh: 瑾，楊溥時謀亂，為徐知訓所殺。

translations.literal: Jin, in Yang Pu's time plotting disorder, was killed by Xu Zhixun.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yang Pu, Jin plotted rebellion and was killed by Xu Zhixun.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰

translations.literal: =The Historiographer says=
translations.idiomatic: The Historiographer's Comment

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：疾風知勁草，世亂見忠臣，誠哉是言也！

translations.literal: The historiographer says: A fierce wind reveals the tough grass; in a chaotic age loyal ministers appear—truly this saying is so!
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Only a storm shows which grass stands firm; only turmoil shows who is truly loyal—how true that old saying is!

sentences.zh: 土運中微，賊巢僭越，籓伯勤王，赴難者，率有聲而無實。

translations.literal: The earth's fortune was in mid-decline; the bandit Chao usurped; feudal lords came to aid the throne—of those who rushed to the crisis, most had reputation without substance.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's mandate was failing; Huang Chao seized power; lords claimed to rescue the throne, yet most who marched to the crisis were all talk and no deed.

sentences.zh: 唯重榮斬賊使於近關，處存舉義師於安喜，橫身泣赴，不顧禍患，遂得義徒雲合，逆黨勢窮。

translations.literal: Only Chongrong beheaded bandit envoys at the near passes and Chucun raised a righteous army at Anxi, throwing themselves forward in tears without regard for calamity; thus righteous followers gathered like clouds and the rebel party's strength was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Only Chongrong executed rebel envoys at the frontier and Chucun raised loyal troops at Anxi, weeping as they threw themselves into danger; righteous men flocked to them and the rebels were driven to ruin.

sentences.zh: 宜乎服冕乘軒，傳家胙土。

translations.literal: It was fitting that they should wear caps and ribbons and ride in high carriages, passing down to their families fief lands and sacrificial meat.
translations.idiomatic: They deserved their honors and the fiefs their sons inherited.

sentences.zh: 而重榮傷於峻法，嚴而少恩，禍發輿臺，誠悲枉橫。

translations.literal: Yet Chongrong was wounded by harsh law—severe and sparing in grace; disaster arose from the carriage platform; truly it is sad that he was wrongly struck down.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chongrong's harsh justice—strict and unforgiving—brought disaster from his own ranks; his wrongful death is pitiable indeed.

sentences.zh: 高駢起家禁旅，頗立功名，玩寇崇妖，致茲狼籍。

translations.literal: Gao Pian rose from the palace guard and won considerable merit, yet he toyed with the bandits and exalted sorcery, bringing about this ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian rose from the palace armies with real achievements, yet he dallied with rebels and courted sorcerers until everything lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 後來勛德，可誡前軍。

translations.literal: Later merit and virtue may warn earlier armies.
translations.idiomatic: Later examples of merit and failure alike should warn those who follow.

sentences.zh: 瑄、溥不以善取，固宜兇終。

translations.literal: Xuan and Pu did not take power by goodness; it was fitting that they should meet violent ends.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and Pu seized power by violence; violent ends were only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 瑾持此狼心，安逃虎口？

translations.literal: Jin harbored this wolf's heart—how could he escape the tiger's maw?
translations.idiomatic: With a heart like a wolf's, how could Jin hope to escape the tiger's jaws?

sentences.zh: 王綱之紊，群盜及茲，復何言哉！

translations.literal: The royal norms were in disorder; bandits in throngs reached this point—what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: When the bonds of kingship unravel and robbers swarm the realm, what more can be said!

sentences.zh: 贊

translations.literal: =Eulogy=
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy

sentences.zh: 贊曰：王者撫運，居安慮危。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: The king who steadies the mandate, dwelling in security, must consider peril.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy reads: A ruler who holds the mandate must, even in peace, reckon with danger.

sentences.zh: 不以德處，即為盜窺。

translations.literal: If he does not dwell in virtue, robbers will spy upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Without virtue in office, bandits already watch and wait.

sentences.zh: 乾坤蕩覆，生聚流離。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth were overturned; the living were scattered and driven into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth were overturned; families were torn apart and driven into exile.

sentences.zh: 讀駢章疏，可為涕洟！

translations.literal: To read Pian's memorials and reports can draw tears and mucus!
translations.idiomatic: To read Pian's memorials is to weep until the tears run dry!
